Reproducing Li, Daie, Svoboda and Druckmann (2016) from dandiset 000011¶

Paper. Li N, Daie K, Svoboda K, Druckmann S (2016). Robust neuronal dynamics in premotor cortex during motor planning. Nature 532, 459-464. doi:10.1038/nature17643. The claims file (claims/000011/10.1038-nature17643.yaml) was written from the HHMI author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC5081260): main text, Methods and the legends of Figures 1 to 6 and Extended Data Figures 1 to 10. The Corrigendum (doi:10.1038/nature18623) was not read.

Dandiset. DANDI:000011, version 0.220126.1907. The paper cites no DANDI version (its data statement points to CRCNS, doi:10.6080/K0RB72JW), so the most recent published version is pinned. It is the only published version. The draft lists the same 92 assets with the same total size (32,435,325,542 bytes); its metadata was modified later (2026-02-12), which the analysis does not use.

What the dandiset holds (shown in the data check below). 91 extracellular files of 19 mice and one empty behaviour file. 58 sessions of 12 mice are the control-mouse recordings of the paper (experiment 1, unilateral photoinhibition, 20 sessions of 4 mice; experiments 2 and 3, bilateral photoinhibition, 38 sessions of 7 and 3 mice). 33 sessions of 7 other mice have no photostimulus record; their subjects and delay match the callosotomy experiment. The behavioural photoinhibition experiments without recordings, the photoactivation mice and the untrained mice used to map photoinhibition are not in the dandiset.

Readings. Where the claims file lists readings of a detail, each is run, and a claim is reproduced when it holds under one of them, as its criterion says. Ten questions were asked about details the claims file did not give (questions/000011.yaml). A reader answered them on 2026-10-21: the paper gives none of them, and the claims file now names readings for each. For most, the readings are method details whose outcomes must agree, else the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified: lick-early trials dropped (K1) or kept (K2) in every neural analysis; the spike counts that set a neuron's preferred trial type (D1 the whole trial, D2 the delay epoch, D3 each bin), the time that labels a bin (L1 its centre, L2 its end) and how far the search for recovery runs (E1 to the go cue, E2 to 1.6 s after it); the selection test and bin of ed4 (s1, s2, t1, t2); the Fisher table of ed6a (f1, f2); the trials whose average cd-captures-selectivity decomposes (v1, v2); the sign of the ramping mode (g1, g2); the noise and step of the modular attractor (n1, n2, h1, h2); and the lick threshold of ed9f. Two answers fix a reading: trials are counted per condition for convention D (N1) and for convention A (T1), and counting per condition and trial type (N2, T2) is shown as a variant. Each section says what its answer changed.

First verification round. A verifier reviewed the attempt on 2026-10-21. In reply, the notebook adds the outputs it asked for (upsampled spike widths, the size of the lick-early artefact under K2, per-neuron trial counts and epoch selectivity of the included populations, per-session ROC of modes 2 and 4, raw lick-trace summaries and example traces, raw levels above the experiment-2 baseline, experiment-3 behaviour and the ed9f test on experiment 3, and the ed10 counts on all trials), and three outcomes changed: selective-fraction and ed2b-silencing-strength are not reproduced (partial before), and cd-stable-over-epochs is blocked as methods_underspecified (reproduced before), as the trials that give w are not fixed. Three new questions were asked (questions/000011.yaml).

The subjects split in two groups. 12 mice (5 VGAT-ChR2-EYFP, 7 PV x ReaChR) with 58 sessions are the control mice of the paper: their counts match the Methods. The 33 sessions of the 7 other mice (6 VGAT, 1 PV x ReaChR) have no photostimulus record at all; the genotype counts and the 1.7 s delay match the callosotomy experiment, but no file says these mice were callosotomised (the subject description holds only the JAX strains). Experiment 1 holds 4 mice here, where Extended Data Fig. 2b gives 6. Three experiment-1 sessions of mouse 255200 have no photostimulus record either. The behaviour-only file holds only metadata.

In every session the sample epoch (pole onset to delay onset) lasts 1.3 s and the delay 1.3 s (experiment 1) or 1.7 s (experiments 2, 3 and the sessions without a photostimulus record), as the Methods say, in trials without an early lick. In early-lick trials the delay restarts, so their delay differs from the nominal one. Session 258250_20141202 holds two interleaved sequences of trial ids whose times overlap (98 overlapping pairs), so its trial events cannot be assigned to trials; it is left out of every trial-based analysis and its units are counted only. Two sessions of mouse 255200 have one or two overlapping pairs and are kept. The trial table has no column for the photostimulus: conditions are read from the laser record below.

The photostimulus of a trial is recorded twice: as photostim_start_time and photostim_stop_time events (the event value is the peak power, mW) and as 5 s chunks of the laser power and AOM traces (10 kHz, 50,000 samples per chunk), one chunk per photostimulus trial, in one series per site (left, right, bilateral). The chunks give the site; the events give the time. The two agree trial by trial: every event with a time has a chunk except in two sessions, and the chunks without an event fall in non-performing trials. Event values below 1 mW (77 events) are kept apart as no_light. The traces separate the protocols of the Methods: a 40 Hz sinusoid of 1.5 mW average for one spot, and a constant power of 1.5 mW per spot when the beam is scanned (3.1 mW for one spot per side, 6.1 mW for four spots on one side, 12.6 mW for four spots per side). Experiment 2 sessions use one spot left or right and eight spots bilaterally; experiment 3 sessions use two spots bilaterally (one per side) and four spots left or right, or one spot left or right in 6 of its 12 sessions.

Experiment 1 holds three conditions, 0.5 s of light ending 1.6 s (sample), 0.8 s (early delay) and 0.3 s (late delay) before the go cue. This settles the naming question of the claims file (convention T): the recorded "late delay" condition ends 0.3 s before the go cue (the Methods' naming); the condition ending at the go cue (the Results' "late delay" of Fig. 1d) is not in the recordings. Experiments 2 and 3 have 0.8 s of light from delay onset. The stop event is 0.5 s or 0.8 s after the start event, so it marks the end of the ramp, the offset the claims file uses.

# Event time against the light in the trace: two sessions read in full
for sid in ["255200_20140913", "263808_20150121"]:
    s = S[sid]; tr = s["trials"]
    aid = assets[assets.path == s["path"]].asset_id.iloc[0]
    rows = []
    with h5py.File(remfile.File(L.s3_url(aid)), "r") as f:
        for site in s["meta"]["sites"]:
            g = f[f"/stimulus/presentation/{site} ALM_laser_power"]
            d, ts = g["data"][:], g["timestamps"][:]
            for r in tr[(tr.ps_site == site) & tr.ps_on.notna() & tr.behaving].itertuples():
                c = int(r.ps_chunk); seg = d[c * 50000:(c + 1) * 50000]; t = ts[c * 50000:(c + 1) * 50000]
                on = np.where(seg > 0.5)[0]
                rows.append({"early_lick": r.early_lick, "event_minus_light_ms": (r.ps_on - t[on[0]]) * 1000 if len(on) else np.nan,
                             "delay_event_minus_light_ms": (r.delay - t[on[0]]) * 1000 if len(on) else np.nan})
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df["mismatch"] = df.event_minus_light_ms.abs() > 20
    print(sid, "trials:", len(df))
    print(df.groupby("early_lick").agg(n=("mismatch", "size"), mismatch=("mismatch", "sum"),
                                       event_minus_light_ms=("event_minus_light_ms", lambda x: f"{x.min():.0f} to {x.max():.0f}")).to_string())

In trials without an early lick the photostimulus event and the light in the trace agree to within 5 ms. In early-lick trials of these two sessions the event is logged up to about 1.6 s (1587 ms) after the light, at the restarted delay, so in those trials the event times do not mark the light. This is one reason the readings below that keep early-lick trials are kept apart.

# Size of the lick-early artefact (verifier's request). Under K2 lick-early trials enter with their
# events at their logged times (claims file, convention K). Per condition: how many lick-early trials
# K2 adds (behaving, correct or incorrect), and where the light seen in the laser trace falls against
# the logged go cue and the logged photostimulus event. Every lick-early photostimulus trial of the
# labelled sessions is read (one 5 s trace chunk per trial).
t0 = time.time()
k2rows = []
for sid, s in S.items():
    if s["exp"] not in ("exp1", "exp2", "exp3"):
        continue
    tr = s["trials"]
    keep = L.trial_mask(tr, "keep")
    e = tr[keep & tr.early_lick.values & tr.ps_site.notna().values & tr.ps_on.notna().values & ~tr.cond.isin(["no_light", "ps_unknown", "control"]).values]
    for c, n in pd.Series(tr.cond[keep]).value_counts().items():
        k2rows.append({"experiment": s["exp"], "sid": sid, "cond": c, "kind": "count", "trials_K2": int(n),
                       "early_K2": int((keep & tr.early_lick.values & (tr.cond == c).values).sum())})
    if len(e):
        aid = assets[assets.path == s["path"]].asset_id.iloc[0]
        lt = L.light_onsets(aid, e)
        for r, x in zip(e.itertuples(), lt):
            k2rows.append({"experiment": s["exp"], "sid": sid, "cond": r.cond, "kind": "light",
                           "light_re_go": x - r.go, "event_re_go": r.ps_on - r.go, "event_minus_light": r.ps_on - x})
k2t = pd.DataFrame(k2rows)
cnt = k2t[k2t.kind == "count"].groupby(["experiment", "cond"])[["trials_K2", "early_K2"]].sum()
cnt["early_fraction"] = (cnt.early_K2 / cnt.trials_K2).round(3)
lt = k2t[k2t.kind == "light"]
q = lt.groupby(["experiment", "cond"]).agg(
    read=("light_re_go", "size"), light_found=("light_re_go", lambda x: int(x.notna().sum())),
    light_re_go=("light_re_go", lambda x: f"{x.min():.2f} / {x.median():.2f} / {x.max():.2f}"),
    event_re_go=("event_re_go", lambda x: f"{x.min():.2f} / {x.median():.2f} / {x.max():.2f}"),
    event_after_light_over_0_1s=("event_minus_light", lambda x: int((x > 0.1).sum())),
    event_minus_light_median_s=("event_minus_light", "median"))
q = q.join(cnt.trials_K2)
q["displaced_fraction_of_condition"] = q.event_after_light_over_0_1s / q.trials_K2
print(f"read in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
print("Trials per condition under K2 (behaving, correct or incorrect) and the lick-early trials among them:")
print(cnt.to_string())
print("\nLick-early photostimulus trials: light onset and logged event re the logged go cue (s; min / median / max),")
print("and how many have the event more than 0.1 s after the light:")
print(q.round(3).to_string())
print("Lick-early photostimulus trials read:", len(lt), "; with the event more than 0.1 s after the light:", int((lt.event_minus_light > 0.1).sum()),
      "; earliest light re the logged go cue (s):", round(lt.light_re_go.min(), 2))

Under K2 the lick-early trials are 15% to 22% of the trials of each condition in experiments 1 and 2, and 7% to 14% in experiment 3. In most of them the light falls where the logged events put it, but in some it came earlier, before one or more restarts of the delay (light as early as 10 s before the logged go cue). Those trials, in which the logged photostimulus event lies more than 0.1 s after the light, are 16% of the sample-epoch condition of experiment 1, 3% to 4% of its other two conditions, 6.5% to 7.5% of each photoinhibition condition of experiment 2 and 1% to 4% in experiment 3 (displaced_fraction_of_condition). In those trials the windows aligned to the logged events miss the light, so K2 mixes trials without photoinhibition into the photoinhibition averages. The K2 readings are run as the claims file defines them (events at their logged times); the claims whose outcome depends on K2 say so. A question asks the reader whether K2 should align those trials to the light in the trace.

The files' cell_type labels follow the same thresholds as the Methods (every unit wider than 0.45 ms is Pyr), except that the units of intermediate width are labelled FS (45 in all; the 15 in the control mice are all 0.358 ms wide). At 19531.25 Hz the width takes discrete values 0.051 ms apart; none falls on a threshold. In 28 units of 3 sessions the spike times are not in time order (the files store them in trial order, and two of these sessions have trials out of time order); they are sorted here. A few spikes (at most 3.3% of a unit's) fall outside the unit's observation intervals.

# Clock check 1: spikes against the photostimulus record. Population rate in the light window
# (onset to offset minus ramp) over the control rate in the same window, and the same with the
# window shifted 1.5 s later (after the light).
rows = []
for sid, s in S.items():
    if s["exp"] not in ("exp1", "exp2", "exp3") or s["meta"]["trials_overlapping"]:
        continue
    tr = s["trials"]; m = L.trial_mask(tr, "drop")
    uu = U[(U.sid == sid) & (U.cls == "pyr")]
    ipsi = {"exp1": ["sample", "early_delay", "late_delay"], "exp2": ["left1"], "exp3": ["left4", "bilateral2"]}[s["exp"]]
    for c in ipsi:
        p = m & (tr.cond == c).values; k = m & (tr.cond == "control").values
        if p.sum() < 3:
            continue
        on, off = np.median(tr.ps_on_re_go[p]), np.median(tr.ps_off_re_go[p]) - (0.1 if s["exp"] == "exp1" else 0.2)
        for shift in (0.0, 1.5):
            a = sum(L.counts_in(u.spikes, tr.go.values[p], on + shift, off + shift).mean() for u in uu.itertuples())
            b = sum(L.counts_in(u.spikes, tr.go.values[k], on + shift, off + shift).mean() for u in uu.itertuples())
            rows.append({"sid": sid, "experiment": s["exp"], "cond": c, "shift_s": shift, "ratio": a / b if b else np.nan})
clk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Population rate, photoinhibition over control, in the light window and 1.5 s later (sessions):")
print(clk.groupby(["experiment", "cond", "shift_s"]).ratio.describe()[["count", "min", "50%", "max"]].round(2).to_string())

# Clock check 2: trial type against spikes. Fraction of putative pyramidal units whose delay-epoch
# counts differ between lick left and lick right control trials (t-test, p < 0.05), with the true
# trial types and with the trial types of the next trial (a shift that breaks the link).
rows = []
for sid, s in S.items():
    if s["meta"]["trials_overlapping"] or s["exp"] == "no_photostim_record" and False:
        continue
    tr = s["trials"]; m = L.trial_mask(tr, "drop", ("hit",)) & tr.cond.isin(["control", "unlabelled"]).values
    if m.sum() < 20:
        continue
    t = tr[m]; right = (t.instruction == "right").values
    shifted = np.roll(right, 1)
    uu = U[(U.sid == sid) & (U.cls == "pyr")]
    for u in uu.itertuples():
        ok = u.observed[m]
        c = L.counts_in(u.spikes, t.go.values, (t.delay - t.go).values, np.zeros(len(t)))
        rows.append({"sid": sid, "experiment": s["exp"], "true": L.ttest(c[ok & right], c[ok & ~right]) < 0.05,
                     "shifted": L.ttest(c[ok & shifted], c[ok & ~shifted]) < 0.05})
dec = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Fraction of units selective in the delay epoch, true against shifted trial types:")
print(dec.groupby("experiment")[["true", "shifted"]].mean().round(3).assign(units=dec.groupby("experiment").size()).to_string())

# Sessions without a photostimulus record: per-trial population rate in the window where the light
# falls in the other sessions (experiment 1: the three windows; otherwise delay onset + 0.0-0.6 s),
# over the session median. Trials below 0.3 are counted; the same count 1.5 s later is the reference.
rows = []
for sid, s in S.items():
    if s["exp"] not in ("no_photostim_record", "exp1_unlabelled"):
        continue
    tr = s["trials"]; m = L.trial_mask(tr, "drop", ("hit", "miss", "ignore"))
    t = tr[m]
    uu = U[(U.sid == sid)]
    if len(t) < 10 or len(uu) == 0:
        rows.append({"sid": sid, "experiment": s["exp"], "trials": len(t)}); continue
    if s["exp"] == "exp1_unlabelled":
        wins = [(-2.1, -1.7), (-1.3, -0.9), (-0.8, -0.4)]
    else:
        wins = [(-1.7, -1.1)]
    out = {"sid": sid, "experiment": s["exp"], "trials": len(t), "units": len(uu)}
    for shift, name in ((0.0, "silenced"), (1.5, "silenced_1.5s_later")):
        low = np.zeros(len(t), bool)
        for a, b in wins:
            pop = sum(L.counts_in(u.spikes, t.go.values, a + shift, b + shift) for u in uu.itertuples())
            med = np.median(pop)
            low |= pop < 0.3 * med if med > 0 else np.zeros(len(t), bool)
        out[name] = round(low.mean(), 2)
    rows.append(out)

The clock checks hold for the 54 sessions with a photostimulus record. In each ipsilateral condition the population rate in the light window has a median over sessions of 0.03 to 0.05 of the control rate (one experiment-2 session reaches 0.70, and one experiment-3 session 1.26 under bilateral light), and 1.5 s later the median is 0.94 to 1.09, so the spikes, the trial events and the photostimulus record share one clock. Delay-epoch selectivity is found in 0.30 to 0.39 of units with the true trial types against 0.06 to 0.09 with those of the next trial, in every group except the three unlabelled experiment-1 sessions (0.33 against 0.23, 30 units).

In most sessions without a photostimulus record, a fraction of trials (up to about 0.4) have their population rate fall below 30% of the session median in the light window of the other sessions, far more than 1.5 s later. These sessions therefore contain photoinhibition trials that no file labels (in a few sessions no such trials appear in this window, so their light, if any, fell elsewhere). Their control trials cannot be told from their photoinhibition trials, so no analysis of them that needs control trials or conditions can be run.

unit-classification¶

1012 single units were recorded in left ALM during behaviour in 58 sessions (20 unilateral, 38 bilateral experiment sessions); by spike width 72 were fast-spiking, 890 putative pyramidal, and 50 intermediate and excluded.

Criterion: width is the trough-to-peak interval of the mean waveform; units and sessions of the control mice only. Reproduced when all values are within tolerance.

Result: partially reproduced. The control mice hold 979 units in 58 sessions (20 unilateral, 38 bilateral), with 74 fast-spiking and 890 putative pyramidal units, all within tolerance; 890 is the paper's number exactly. Only 15 units have intermediate widths, against 50: the dandiset holds 33 units fewer than the paper's 1012, about the number of intermediate units missing (35), so the intermediate units were probably left out of the deposit.

With widths from waveforms interpolated to ten times the stored rate (a variant), 11 units are intermediate, 79 fast-spiking and 889 putative pyramidal, so the 19.5 kHz sampling does not explain the shortfall of intermediate units. The criterion defines no partial outcome; four of its five values hold, so the outcome is partial by the rule given in the Summary.

selective-fraction¶

Most putative pyramidal neurons distinguished trial types (634 of 890); 176 in the sample epoch, 337 in the delay epoch and 493 in the response epoch.

Criterion: convention S on the putative pyramidal neurons, control trials; reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance under one combination of readings: response epoch 1.3 s (R1) or 1.5 s (R2) after the go cue; correct trials (O1) or correct and incorrect (O2); Student's or Welch's t-test. Lick-early trials are dropped (K1) or kept (K2); the answer (convention K) found the paper silent, so the outcome must hold under both. The 44 putative pyramidal units of the three experiment-1 sessions without a photostimulus record have no identifiable control trials; they are left out, and shown as a variant with all their trials.

Result: not reproduced. On the 846 putative pyramidal units whose control trials can be identified, no combination of readings brings all four counts within tolerance. With lick-early trials dropped (K1) only the response-epoch count reaches its band (445 or 446 under three readings with correct trials only); the counts in any epoch (at most 565, band 571 to 697), in the sample epoch (at most 156, band 158 to 194) and in the delay epoch (at most 294, band 303 to 371) fall short. With lick-early trials kept (K2) three of four reach their bands under the four readings with correct trials only (any epoch 575 to 588, delay 315 to 320, response 453 to 464), and the sample count does not (at most 149). The outcome must be the one K1 and K2 both give, and under K1 only one of the four counts holds, so the claim is not reproduced (the first round gave partial; the rule is in the Summary). Most units are selective all the same (563 of 846 with K1, R1 and correct trials). With the 44 units of the three unlabelled sessions added on all their trials, which include photoinhibition trials and so are not the control trials the criterion names, all four counts are within tolerance with correct trials and K1 (592, 165, 307 and 464 with R1 and Student's test) and under no reading with K2.

Behaviour during the recordings (variant for blocked claims)¶

fig1d-late-delay-ipsilateral-bias, fig1d-earlier-photoinhibition-minimal, ed3-behaviour-recovery-interval and the two fig2b claims rest on the paper's behavioural photoinhibition experiments (5 and 13 mice, photoinhibition on 25% of trials, conditions not in the recordings such as light ending at the go cue, 1.3 s photoinhibition and four-spot unilateral photoinhibition). Those sessions are not in the dandiset, so the claims are blocked. The behaviour recorded during the electrophysiology sessions is shown here for reference only; it is a different set of sessions and does not decide an outcome.

In [17]:
def perf(tr, cond, side=None, ignore_as_error=False):
    m = tr.behaving & ~tr.early_lick & (tr.cond == cond)
    if not ignore_as_error:
        m &= tr.outcome.isin(["hit", "miss"])
    if side:
        m &= tr.instruction == side
    t = tr[m]
    return (t.outcome == "hit").mean() if len(t) else np.nan, len(t)

rows = []
for s in S.values():
    if s["exp"] not in ("exp1", "exp2"):
        continue
    for c in ["control", "sample", "early_delay", "late_delay", "left1", "right1", "bilateral8"]:
        p, n = perf(s["trials"], c)
        pr, _ = perf(s["trials"], c, "right")
        if n:
            rows.append({"experiment": s["exp"], "subject": s["subject"], "cond": c, "perf": p, "perf_right": pr, "n": n})
bp = pd.DataFrame(rows)
mouse = bp.groupby(["experiment", "subject", "cond"]).apply(lambda d: pd.Series({"perf": np.average(d.perf, weights=d.n), "perf_right": np.nanmean(d.perf_right)})).reset_index()
for exp, conds in [("exp1", ["sample", "early_delay", "late_delay"]), ("exp2", ["left1", "right1", "bilateral8"])]:
    m = mouse[mouse.experiment == exp].pivot(index="subject", columns="cond", values="perf")
    print(f"{exp}: performance per mouse (fraction correct, lick-early excluded)")
    print(m.round(3).to_string())
    for c in conds:
        tp = stats.ttest_rel(m[c], m["control"]).pvalue
        ti = stats.ttest_ind(m[c], m["control"]).pvalue
        print(f"  {c}: mean {m[c].mean():.3f} against control {m['control'].mean():.3f}; paired p = {tp:.3g}, unpaired p = {ti:.3g}")

# Experiment 3 behaviour per mouse (verifier's request; reference only), and one-spot unilateral
# photoinhibition with the two hemispheres pooled per mouse (trials of left1 and right1 together).
rows = []
for s in S.values():
    if s["exp"] not in ("exp2", "exp3"):
        continue
    tr = s["trials"]
    for c in ["control", "left1", "right1", "left4", "right4", "bilateral2", "bilateral8", "one spot pooled"]:
        cc = ["left1", "right1"] if c == "one spot pooled" else [c]
        m = tr.behaving & ~tr.early_lick & tr.cond.isin(cc) & tr.outcome.isin(["hit", "miss"])
        if m.sum():
            rows.append({"experiment": s["exp"], "subject": s["subject"], "cond": c, "hits": int((tr.outcome[m] == "hit").sum()), "n": int(m.sum())})
bq = pd.DataFrame(rows).groupby(["experiment", "subject", "cond"])[["hits", "n"]].sum().reset_index()
bq["perf"] = bq.hits / bq.n
for exp in ("exp3", "exp2"):
    m = bq[bq.experiment == exp].pivot(index="subject", columns="cond", values="perf")
    nn = bq[bq.experiment == exp].groupby("cond").n.sum().to_dict()
    print(f"\n{exp}: performance per mouse (trials pooled over sessions, lick-early excluded); trials per condition {nn}")
    print(m.round(3).to_string())
    for c in [x for x in m.columns if x != "control"]:
        d = m[[c, "control"]].dropna()
        if len(d) >= 2:
            print(f"  {c}: mean {d[c].mean():.3f} against control {d['control'].mean():.3f} over {len(d)} mice; "
                  f"paired p = {stats.ttest_rel(d[c], d['control']).pvalue:.3g}, unpaired p = {stats.ttest_ind(d[c], d['control']).pvalue:.3g}")
print("\nPaper (Fig. 2b, 13 mice of the behavioural cohort): one spot 70.3%, four spots 67.7%, bilateral two spots 58.0%, eight spots 51.4%.")

ed4-return-to-trajectory¶

Neurons whose spike rates decreased during the delay epoch also recovered after unilateral photoinhibition, returning to the time-matched control trajectory and not decaying to the end-point rate.

Criterion: experiment 1; neurons with a significant decrease of the spike count in the last 400 ms of the delay against the first 400 ms (two-tailed t-test, p < 0.05, trial types pooled); rates normalised to the neuron's mean rate; for each condition the RMS between photoinhibition offset and the go cue of the perturbed minus time-matched control rate and of the perturbed rate minus the control rate at the end of the delay; readings (a) one value per neuron averaged over conditions and trial types, (b) one per neuron, condition and trial type; reproduced when the time-matched RMS is smaller by a paired t-test with p < 0.001 under a reading. Answered 2026-10-21 as not given by the paper: the selection test paired (s1) or unpaired (s2), the bin of the rate time course 200 ms (t1) or 400 ms (t2), and lick-early trials dropped (K1) or kept (K2); the outcome must hold under all, and the count of 27 is reported against each. Neurons are the putative pyramidal neurons (convention U); trials are correct and incorrect ones; the mean rate is over control trials from sample onset to 1.3 s after the go cue.

In [18]:
OFF1 = {"sample": -1.6, "early_delay": -0.8, "late_delay": -0.3}
e1 = U[(U.exp == "exp1") & (U.cls == "pyr")]
ed4_rows, ed4_detail = [], {}
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for paired in (True, False):
        chosen = []
        for u in e1.itertuples():
            tr = S[u.sid]["trials"]
            m = L.trial_mask(tr, early) & (tr.cond == "control").values & u.observed
            t = tr[m]
            a = L.counts_in(u.spikes, t.go.values, (t.delay - t.go).values, (t.delay - t.go).values + 0.4)
            b = L.counts_in(u.spikes, t.go.values, -0.4, 0.0)
            if len(t) < 3:
                continue
            p = stats.ttest_rel(b, a).pvalue if paired else stats.ttest_ind(b, a).pvalue
            if p < 0.05 and b.mean() < a.mean():
                chosen.append(u.uid)
        for w in (0.2, 0.4):
            sub = e1[e1.uid.isin(chosen)]
            rm = L.rate_matrices(sub, S, w, early)
            tl = L.labels(w, "centre")
            j_end = int(np.argmin(abs(L.GRID_END - 0.0)))     # window ending at the go cue
            per = []
            for uid, d in rm.items():
                ctrl = d["cond"] == "control"
                so = d["so"][ctrl]
                n_all = L.counts_in(d["spikes"], d["go"][ctrl], so, np.full(ctrl.sum(), 1.3))
                mean_rate = n_all.sum() / np.sum(1.3 - so)
                if mean_rate <= 0:
                    continue
                for c, off in OFF1.items():
                    win = (tl > off) & (tl <= 0)
                    for side in (True, False):
                        pm = (d["cond"] == c) & (d["right"] == side)
                        cm = ctrl & (d["right"] == side)
                        if pm.sum() < 1 or cm.sum() < 1:
                            continue
                        rp = d["rate"][pm].mean(0) / mean_rate
                        rc = d["rate"][cm].mean(0) / mean_rate
                        per.append({"uid": uid, "cond": c, "right": side,
                                    "rms_matched": np.sqrt(np.mean((rp[win] - rc[win]) ** 2)),
                                    "rms_endpoint": np.sqrt(np.mean((rp[win] - rc[j_end]) ** 2))})
            per = pd.DataFrame(per)
            ed4_detail[(early, paired, w)] = per
            avg = per.groupby("uid")[["rms_matched", "rms_endpoint"]].mean()
            ta = stats.ttest_rel(avg.rms_matched, avg.rms_endpoint)
            tb = stats.ttest_rel(per.rms_matched, per.rms_endpoint)
            ed4_rows.append({"early_lick": early, "selection_test": "paired" if paired else "unpaired", "bin_s": w,
                             "neurons": len(chosen), "mice": sub.subject.nunique(),
                             "a_matched": avg.rms_matched.mean(), "a_endpoint": avg.rms_endpoint.mean(), "a_t": ta.statistic, "a_p": ta.pvalue,
                             "b_n": len(per), "b_matched": per.rms_matched.mean(), "b_endpoint": per.rms_endpoint.mean(), "b_t": tb.statistic, "b_p": tb.pvalue})
ed4 = pd.DataFrame(ed4_rows)
ed4["holds_a"] = (ed4.a_p < 0.001) & (ed4.a_matched < ed4.a_endpoint)
ed4["holds_b"] = (ed4.b_p < 0.001) & (ed4.b_matched < ed4.b_endpoint)
print(ed4.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("\nPaper: 27 neurons from 6 mice (tolerance 2.7), paired t-test p < 0.001.")

Paper: 27 neurons from 6 mice (tolerance 2.7), paired t-test p < 0.001.

Result: not reproduced. The selection finds 47 to 67 putative pyramidal neurons with a significant delay-epoch decrease, from 4 mice (paper 27 from 6). Under no reading is the RMS of the difference from the time-matched control smaller than the RMS of the difference from the end-point rate: the two are within 0.02 of each other in every row (paired p 0.41 to 0.98 with one value per neuron, 0.30 to 0.98 with one value per neuron, condition and trial type). This holds under all eight combinations of s1, s2, t1, t2, K1 and K2 that the answer requires, so the outcome is unchanged.

fig1f-spike-rate-recovery¶

Within 400 ms after unilateral photoinhibition, spike rates became indistinguishable from control in 90% of neurons; 10% retained a sustained change.

Criterion: convention R on putative pyramidal neurons of experiment 1, per condition; the fraction of neurons with a significant change (p < 0.01) in the 400 ms window at 400 ms after photoinhibition offset; readings (a) each of the three conditions, (b) the three pooled; window labelled by its end (W1) or centre (W2); neurons below 1 spike/s or with fewer than 3 trials excluded (X1) or not (X2). Reproduced when the fraction is within 0.09 to 0.11 under one combination. Lick-early trials dropped (K1) or kept (K2); answered 2026-10-21 as not given by the paper, the outcome must hold under both.

In [19]:
f1_rows = []
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for X in ("X1", "X2"):
        res_c = {}
        for c, off in OFF1.items():
            P, info = L.rate_change_tests(e1, S, c, 0.4, early, min_rate=1 if X == "X1" else None, min_trials=3 if X == "X1" else None)
            res_c[c] = (P, info)
        for lab in ("end", "centre"):
            tl = L.labels(0.4, lab)
            tot_sig = tot_n = 0
            row = {"early_lick": early, "exclusion": X, "label": "W1 end" if lab == "end" else "W2 centre"}
            for c, off in OFF1.items():
                P, info = res_c[c]
                inc = info.included.values & ~np.isnan(P).all(1)
                j = int(np.argmin(abs(tl - (off + 0.4))))
                sig = P[inc, j] < 0.01
                row[f"n_{c}"] = int(inc.sum()); row[f"frac_{c}"] = sig.mean()
                jd = int(np.argmin(abs(tl - off)))
                row[f"during_{c}"] = (P[inc, jd] < 0.01).mean()
                tot_sig += sig.sum(); tot_n += inc.sum()
            row["frac_pooled"] = tot_sig / tot_n
            f1_rows.append(row)
f1 = pd.DataFrame(f1_rows)
f1["a_each_within"] = f1[[f"frac_{c}" for c in OFF1]].sub(0.1).abs().le(0.01 + 1e-12).all(axis=1)
f1["b_pooled_within"] = (f1.frac_pooled - 0.1).abs() <= 0.01 + 1e-12
print(f1.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nPaper: n = 168, 168, 175 neurons; fraction 0.10 (tolerance 0.01). 'during_' is the fraction at the window labelled at offset.")

Result: reproduced. With windows labelled by their centre and no exclusion (W2, X2), the pooled fraction of neurons with a significant change 400 ms after offset is 0.101 with lick-early trials dropped and 0.097 with them kept, both within 0.09 to 0.11, so it holds under K1 and K2 as the answer requires. The per-condition fractions under that reading are 0.105, 0.113 and 0.085 (dropped), so reading (a) does not hold; with the exclusion (X1) 170 to 172 neurons are tested per condition (paper 168 to 175) and the pooled fraction is 0.112 to 0.165. During the light 27% to 72% of neurons are significant, depending on the window label. The passing reading is the one without the exclusion, and it tests 248 neurons per condition, against the paper's 168 to 175; the reading with the exclusion (X1) comes close to the paper's counts (170 to 172) and fails. The criterion allows either, so the outcome is reproduced, but it rests on the reading whose neuron count differs from the paper's.

fig1g-selectivity-recovery¶

After unilateral photoinhibition ALM neurons recovered more than 80% of their control selectivity within about 0.5 s; recovery times were 373 ms (sample), 510 ms (early delay) and 327 ms (late delay).

Criterion: convention D on experiment 1 (selective neurons tested on more than 3 trials in every condition; preferred trial type from 10 random control trials, redrawn 20 times and averaged; selectivity on correct and incorrect trials grouped by instruction); recovery time is the first window after photoinhibition offset where the population selectivity on photoinhibition trials reaches 80% of the time-matched control selectivity; bins of 200 ms (B1) or 400 ms (B2) in 50 ms steps. Reproduced when all three times are within the paper's s.e.m. under one bin reading; partially for two of three. The selective neurons are those of selective-fraction under each of its readings. Answered 2026-10-21, none given by the paper: lick-early trials (K1 dropped, K2 kept); the window of the preference counts (D1 whole trial, D2 delay epoch, D3 each bin); the label of a bin (L1 centre, L2 end); the end of the search (E1 the go cue, E2 1.6 s after it, the end of the windows; the paper's late-delay time of 327 ms after an offset 0.3 s before the go cue falls after the go cue). The outcome is the one all of them give, else methods_underspecified. Trials are counted per condition (N1, the legend's words); per condition and trial type (N2) is a variant. The measured time is that of the population of all included neurons; the bootstrap (200 resamples of neurons) mean and s.d. are shown beside it.

# Population sizes (verifier's request, reference only). For the included neurons of convention D
# (selective under reading R1-O1-student, more than 3 trials in every condition, N1), the fewest trials
# a neuron has in any condition, and the epochs in which it is selective. This does not change the
# selection, which the claims file fixes; it shows which further selections would bring the counts
# near the paper's 55, 143 and 40.
def included_neurons(units, conds, early, skey="R1-O1-student"):
    st = tests[(early, skey)].set_index("uid")
    rows = []
    for u in units[units.uid.isin(SEL[early][skey])].itertuples():
        tr = S[u.sid]["trials"]
        m = L.trial_mask(tr, early) & u.observed
        right = (tr.instruction == "right").values
        n = {}
        ok = True
        for c in ("control",) + tuple(conds):
            mc = m & (tr.cond == c).values
            n[c] = int(mc.sum())
            ok &= mc.sum() > 3 and (mc & right).sum() > 0 and (mc & ~right).sum() > 0
        if ok:
            p = st.loc[u.uid]
            rows.append({"uid": u.uid, "subject": u.subject, "min_trials": min(n.values()),
                         "min_trials_per_type": min(min(int((m & (tr.cond == c).values & right).sum()), int((m & (tr.cond == c).values & ~right).sum()))
                                                    for c in ("control",) + tuple(conds)),
                         "sample": p["sample"] < 0.05, "delay": p["delay"] < 0.05, "response": p["response"] < 0.05})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
prow = []
for name, units_, conds, paper in (("exp1 (fig1g)", e1, list(OFF1), 55), ("exp2 (fig2e)", U[(U.exp == "exp2") & (U.cls == "pyr")], ["left1", "right1", "bilateral8"], 143),
                                   ("exp3 (ed7)", U[(U.exp == "exp3") & (U.cls == "pyr")], ["left4", "right4", "bilateral2"], 40)):
    for early in ("drop", "keep"):
        d = included_neurons(units_, conds, early)
        prow.append({"experiment": name, "early_lick": early, "paper": paper, "included": len(d), "mice": d.subject.nunique(),
                     "min_trials_q10_q50_q90": "/".join(str(int(x)) for x in d.min_trials.quantile([0.1, 0.5, 0.9])),
                     "min_trials_gt_10": int((d.min_trials > 10).sum()), "min_trials_gt_20": int((d.min_trials > 20).sum()),
                     "per_type_gt_3": int((d.min_trials_per_type > 3).sum()), "per_type_gt_5": int((d.min_trials_per_type > 5).sum()),
                     "sel_sample": int(d["sample"].sum()), "sel_delay": int(d.delay.sum()), "sel_response": int(d.response.sum()),
                     "delay_only": int((d.delay & ~d["sample"] & ~d.response).sum()), "sample_or_delay": int((d["sample"] | d.delay).sum()),
                     "sample_and_delay": int((d["sample"] & d.delay).sum())})
print(pd.DataFrame(prow).to_string(index=False))

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The answer confirmed that the paper gives none of the details asked about, and the claims file now requires one outcome over all of them (K1, K2; D1 to D3; L1, L2; E1, E2), with trials counted per condition (N1). They give different outcomes: of the 24 combinations, 12 have readings with all three recovery times within tolerance, 9 have readings with two and 3 have none. With lick-early trials dropped, all three are within tolerance under every combination whose search runs past the go cue (E2), and under E1 with centre labels; E1 with end labels reaches two. With lick-early trials kept, three combinations reach none (end labels with whole-trial preference under E1 and E2, and with delay-epoch preference under E1). Counting trials per condition and trial type (N2, a variant) gives 11 combinations with all three, 12 with two and 1 with none. Every reading includes 138 to 173 neurons, against the paper's 55.

Under E1 with end labels the late-delay time is never found (NaN in all 96 readings): no bin up to the go cue reaches 80% of control. The paper's 327 ms falls 27 ms after the go cue for this condition (offset 0.3 s before it), so a search ending at the go cue can give at most 300 ms, which is inside the tolerance (215 to 439 ms); a question asks the reader whether E1 is meant for this condition. Population sizes (reference only): of the 162 neurons included with K1 (R1-O1-Student), the fewest trials in any condition has a median of 27 (10th percentile 11); 118 have more than 20 trials in every condition, 73 are selective in the delay epoch, 95 in the sample or delay epoch and 15 in the delay epoch only. None of these selections gives the paper's 55, and the same holds for experiment 2 (286 included, 160 delay-selective, 113 with more than 20 trials; paper 143) and experiment 3 (58, 34, 46; paper 40).

ed2b-silencing-strength¶

Ipsilateral and bilateral photoinhibition reduced the activity of putative pyramidal neurons by more than 90%, similarly in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP and PV x ReaChR mice; contralateral photoinhibition had little effect on the average rate.

Criterion: per neuron (mean rate at least 1 spike/s), the rate during photoinhibition over the control rate in the same window; window (a) the whole photostimulus before the ramp, (b) the last 400 ms of photoinhibition. Reproduced when the mean normalised rate is below 0.1 for ipsilateral photoinhibition in both mouse lines (experiment 2) and for bilateral photoinhibition, and contralateral photoinhibition leaves it above 0.8. Judged on experiment 2; experiments 1 and 3 are shown. Neurons need 2 trials in the condition and in control (a standard choice); trials are correct and incorrect ones; lick-early trials dropped (K1) or kept (K2), answered 2026-10-21 as not given by the paper, so the outcome must hold under both.

CONDS = {"exp1": {"sample": "ipsilateral", "early_delay": "ipsilateral", "late_delay": "ipsilateral"},
         "exp2": {"left1": "ipsilateral", "right1": "contralateral", "bilateral8": "bilateral"},
         "exp3": {"left4": "ipsilateral", "right4": "contralateral", "bilateral2": "bilateral"}}
RAMP = {"exp1": 0.1, "exp2": 0.2, "exp3": 0.2}
rows = []
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for exp, cmap in CONDS.items():
        uu = U[(U.exp == exp) & (U.cls == "pyr")]
        for u in uu.itertuples():
            tr = S[u.sid]["trials"]
            m = L.trial_mask(tr, early) & u.observed
            k = m & (tr.cond == "control").values
            so = (tr["sample"] - tr.go).values[k]
            n_all = L.counts_in(u.spikes, tr.go.values[k], so, np.full(k.sum(), 1.3))
            mean_rate = n_all.sum() / np.sum(1.3 - so) if k.sum() else 0
            if mean_rate < 1:
                continue
            for c, kind in cmap.items():
                p = m & (tr.cond == c).values
                if p.sum() < 2 or k.sum() < 2:
                    continue
                on, off = np.median(tr.ps_on_re_go.values[p & ~tr.early_lick.values]), np.median(tr.ps_off_re_go.values[p & ~tr.early_lick.values])
                for wname, (a, b) in {"a": (on, off - RAMP[exp]), "b": (off - 0.4, off)}.items():
                    cp = L.counts_in(u.spikes, tr.go.values[p], a, b).mean()
                    cc = L.counts_in(u.spikes, tr.go.values[k], a, b).mean()
                    rows.append({"early_lick": early, "experiment": exp, "cond": c, "kind": kind, "window": wname,
                                 "genotype": u.genotype, "uid": u.uid, "norm": cp / cc if cc > 0 else np.nan})
nr = pd.DataFrame(rows)
tab = nr.groupby(["early_lick", "window", "experiment", "cond", "kind"]).norm.agg(["size", "mean", "sem"]).round(3)

Result: not reproduced. Photoinhibition silences most activity, but not by more than 90% in every case. With lick-early trials dropped (K1), the normalised rate in experiment 2 is 0.077 to 0.097 for bilateral and 0.94 to 1.00 for contralateral photoinhibition, and 0.035 to 0.052 for ipsilateral photoinhibition in PV x ReaChR mice, but 0.177 to 0.245 in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice: three of the four parts hold. With lick-early trials kept (K2) only the contralateral part holds (1.01 to 1.04); ipsilateral photoinhibition leaves 0.139 to 0.140 (PV) and 0.282 to 0.356 (VGAT), and bilateral 0.169 to 0.196. The outcome must be the one K1 and K2 both give, and under K2 one part of four holds, so the claim is not reproduced (the first round gave partial; the rule is in the Summary). Part of the K2 rise comes from lick-early trials whose light falls before its logged time, 6.5% to 7.5% of the experiment-2 photoinhibition trials (data check), which enter the photoinhibition average without light in the window. Experiment 1 gives 0.037 to 0.098 (K1). Neuron counts are 172, 299 and 55 to 110 per condition, against 109 to 117, 294 to 301 and 52 to 102. Neurons need 2 trials in the condition and in control, a standard choice.

ed2e-no-rebound¶

No rebound excitation was detected on average after photoinhibition offset; a small fraction of neurons showed rebound, balanced by weak sustained inhibition in a larger fraction.

Criterion: experiment 2, photoinhibition 0.8 s at delay onset, lick right trials only, the six 400 ms windows of the legend; per neuron control against photoinhibition by two-tailed t-test, p < 0.01. Reproduced when, in the first 400 ms and 400 to 800 ms after photoinhibition (ipsilateral), the population mean rate is not higher than control (paired t-test across neurons, p > 0.05, a reading) and fewer neurons have a significant increase than a significant decrease. Neurons: putative pyramidal with at least 2 lick right trials in each condition (a standard choice); lick-early trials dropped (K1) or kept (K2), answered 2026-10-21 as not given by the paper, so the outcome must hold under both.

for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for c in ("left1", "right1", "bilateral8"):

            tr = S[u.sid]["trials"]
            m = L.trial_mask(tr, early) & u.observed & (tr.instruction == "right").values
            k, p = m & (tr.cond == "control").values, m & (tr.cond == c).values
            if k.sum() < 2 or p.sum() < 2:
                continue
            for wn, (a, b) in WIN.items():
                cc = L.counts_in(u.spikes, tr.go.values[k], a, b) / (b - a)
                cp = L.counts_in(u.spikes, tr.go.values[p], a, b) / (b - a)

def summ(d):
    t = stats.ttest_rel(d.pi, d.ctrl)

ed6a-bilateral-inconsistent-bias¶

Bilateral photoinhibition biased movements inconsistently across mice and sessions, toward lick left in some and lick right in others.

Criterion: per session of the bilateral experiment, bias = (lick right minus lick left performance) under bilateral photoinhibition minus the same in control; reproduced when, among sessions with a bias significant by Fisher's exact test (p < 0.05), both signs occur, in at least two mice. Which 2 x 2 table enters Fisher's test was answered 2026-10-21 as not given by the paper; readings (f1, printed as p_i) bilateral trials, trial type by correct; (f2, printed as p_ii) licked side by condition (control against bilateral); the outcome must hold under both. Experiment 2 sessions (bilateral photoinhibition of four spots per side); performance excludes lick-early trials (convention P) and no-response trials (shown with them counted as errors as a variant). Experiment 3 (one spot per side) is shown as a variant.

In [25]:
def session_bias(tr, bil, ignore_as_error=False):
    outs = ("hit", "miss", "ignore") if ignore_as_error else ("hit", "miss")
    m = tr.behaving & ~tr.early_lick & tr.outcome.isin(outs)
    out = {}
    for c in ("control", bil):
        t = tr[m & (tr.cond == c)]
        r, l = t[t.instruction == "right"], t[t.instruction == "left"]
        out[c] = dict(pr=(r.outcome == "hit").mean(), pl=(l.outcome == "hit").mean(),
                      rh=int((r.outcome == "hit").sum()), rn=len(r), lh=int((l.outcome == "hit").sum()), ln=len(l),
                      lick_right=int(((t.instruction == "right") & (t.outcome == "hit")).sum() + ((t.instruction == "left") & (t.outcome != "hit")).sum()),
                      n=len(t))
    b, c = out[bil], out["control"]
    bias = (b["pr"] - b["pl"]) - (c["pr"] - c["pl"])
    p_i = stats.fisher_exact([[b["rh"], b["rn"] - b["rh"]], [b["lh"], b["ln"] - b["lh"]]]).pvalue
    p_ii = stats.fisher_exact([[b["lick_right"], b["n"] - b["lick_right"]], [c["lick_right"], c["n"] - c["lick_right"]]]).pvalue
    return bias, p_i, p_ii, b["n"]

rows = []
for s in S.values():
    for exp, bil in (("exp2", "bilateral8"), ("exp3", "bilateral2")):
        if s["exp"] != exp or not s["trials"].behaving.any():
            continue
        for ign in (False, True):
            bias, p_i, p_ii, n = session_bias(s["trials"], bil, ign)
            rows.append({"experiment": exp, "sid": s["sid"], "subject": s["subject"], "ignore_as_error": ign, "bilateral_trials": n,
                         "bias": bias, "p_i": p_i, "p_ii": p_ii})

              f"both signs, in at least two mice in all: {len(pos) > 0 and len(neg) > 0 and sig.subject.nunique() >= 2}; "
              f"each sign in at least two mice: {pos.subject.nunique() >= 2 and neg.subject.nunique() >= 2}")

fig2e-selectivity-recovery-times¶

Selectivity recovered to 80% of control 538 ms after ipsilateral and 192 ms after contralateral photoinhibition, and did not recover after bilateral photoinhibition.

Criterion: convention D on experiment 2 (ipsilateral one spot, contralateral one spot, bilateral four spots per side; light 0.8 s from delay onset, offset 0.9 s before the go cue). Bilateral, no recovery means photoinhibition selectivity below 80% of control up to the go cue. Reproduced when both times are within tolerance and bilateral does not recover, under one bin reading. The method details answered 2026-10-21 (K, D, L, E) are run as for fig1g, and the outcome must be the same under all; trials per condition (N1) decide, per condition and trial type (N2) is a variant.

N1: ipsilateral time 1000.0 to 2400.0 ms (no recovery in 212 of 384 ); contralateral 200.00000000000006 to 1300.0 ms; bilateral below 80% up to the go cue in 384 of 384
Included neurons, N1: 260 to 293 ; N2: 221 to 292 ; paper 143 (tolerance 14.3)

Result: not reproduced. Under all 24 combinations of the method details (K1, K2; D1 to D3; L1, L2; E1, E2), with trials per condition (N1), no reading puts both times within tolerance, so the outcome is the same under all and the answers leave it unchanged. With the search past the go cue (E2), ipsilateral selectivity reaches 80% of control 1000 to 2400 ms after offset, after the go cue, or not at all (20 of 192 readings); with the search ending at the go cue (E1) it never does. The paper gives 538 ms. Contralateral selectivity reaches 80% of control 200 to 1300 ms after offset (paper 192 ms), within tolerance under some readings. Bilateral selectivity stays below 80% of control up to the go cue under all 384 readings. 260 to 293 neurons are included with trials per condition (221 to 292 per condition and trial type), against the paper's 143.

fig2-recordings-recovery¶

After ipsilateral (one spot) photoinhibition spike rate (more than 90%) and selectivity (more than 80%) recovered within 600 ms; contralateral photoinhibition hardly affected activity; after bilateral photoinhibition spike rates recovered on average but selectivity did not.

Criterion: experiment 2, at 600 ms after photoinhibition offset (0.3 s before the go cue). Spike rate recovery (a) fewer than 10% of neurons with a significant change (convention R), (b) population mean rate at least 90% of control. Selectivity (convention D) at least 80% of control. Contralateral: fewer than 10% of neurons significant in every window during and after photoinhibition. Bilateral: rate recovered as in (a) or (b), and selectivity below 80% of control at the go cue. Reproduced when all hold under one combination of the claim's readings (R: W1, W2, X1, X2; D: bins and the S readings). The method details answered 2026-10-21 (K1, K2; D1 to D3; L1, L2) must give the same outcome; trials are counted per condition (N1). The search end (E) does not enter, as no recovery time is read.

R2 = {}
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for X in ("X1", "X2"):
        for c in OFF2:
            R2[(early, X, c)] = L.rate_change_tests(e2, S, c, 0.4, early, min_rate=1 if X == "X1" else None, min_trials=3 if X == "X1" else None)
rate_rows = []
for (early, X, c), (P, info) in R2.items():
    inc = info.included.values & ~np.isnan(P).all(1)
    for lab in ("end", "centre"):
        tl = L.labels(0.4, lab)
        j = int(np.argmin(abs(tl - (-0.9 + 0.6))))
        during_after = (tl >= -1.7 + 0.2) & (tl <= 0) if lab == "centre" else (tl >= -1.7 + 0.4) & (tl <= 0)
        frac_t = np.nanmean(P[inc] < 0.01, axis=0)
        rate_rows.append({"early_lick": early, "exclusion": X, "cond": c, "label": lab, "n": int(inc.sum()),
                          "frac_sig_600ms": frac_t[j], "max_frac_sig_during_after": frac_t[during_after].max()})
rr = pd.DataFrame(rate_rows)
# population mean rate at 600 ms after offset, photoinhibition over control (same windows)
pop_rows = []
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for lab in ("end", "centre"):
        tl = L.labels(0.4, lab); j = int(np.argmin(abs(tl - (-0.3))))
        for c in OFF2:
            num = den = 0.0
            for u in e2.itertuples():
                tr = S[u.sid]["trials"]; m = L.trial_mask(tr, early) & u.observed
                k, p = m & (tr.cond == "control").values, m & (tr.cond == c).values
                if k.sum() < 2 or p.sum() < 2:
                    continue
                e = L.GRID_END[j]
                num += L.counts_in(u.spikes, tr.go.values[p], e - 0.4, e).mean(); den += L.counts_in(u.spikes, tr.go.values[k], e - 0.4, e).mean()
            pop_rows.append({"early_lick": early, "label": lab, "cond": c, "pop_rate_ratio_600ms": num / den})
pr = pd.DataFrame(pop_rows)
print(rr.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(pr.round(3).to_string(index=False))

# selectivity ratio (photoinhibition over control) at 600 ms after offset and at the go cue
sel_rows = []
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for key, (tl, cm) in courses2[early].items():
        w, pw, pt, sk, lab = key
        j600 = int(np.argmin(abs(tl - (-0.3)))); jgo = int(np.argmin(abs(tl - 0.0)))
        sel_rows.append({"early_lick": early, "bin": w, "pref": pw, "trials_rule": "per type" if pt else "per condition", "S": sk, "label": lab,
                         "ipsi_sel_ratio_600ms": cm["left1"][j600] / cm["control"][j600],
                         "bilateral_sel_ratio_go": cm["bilateral8"][jgo] / cm["control"][jgo]})
sr = pd.DataFrame(sel_rows)
# rate parts: claim readings W (window label of convention R) and X; selectivity parts: claim readings B and S,
# method details K, D and L (the label of the selectivity bins), N1 deciding
rate_parts = []
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for W in ("end", "centre"):
        for X in ("X1", "X2"):
            r = rr[(rr.early_lick == early) & (rr.label == W) & (rr.exclusion == X)].set_index("cond")
            p = pr[(pr.early_lick == early) & (pr.label == W)].set_index("cond")
            rate_parts.append({"early_lick": early, "W": W, "X": X,
                               "ipsi_rate": (r.loc["left1", "frac_sig_600ms"] < 0.10) or (p.loc["left1", "pop_rate_ratio_600ms"] >= 0.9),
                               "bilateral_rate": (r.loc["bilateral8", "frac_sig_600ms"] < 0.10) or (p.loc["bilateral8", "pop_rate_ratio_600ms"] >= 0.9),
                               "contra_hardly_affected": r.loc["right1", "max_frac_sig_during_after"] < 0.10})
rate_parts = pd.DataFrame(rate_parts)
print(rate_parts.to_string(index=False))
out = []
for rule in ("per condition", "per type"):
    for (early, pw, lab), d in sr[sr.trials_rule == rule].groupby(["early_lick", "pref", "label"]):
        rp = rate_parts[rate_parts.early_lick == early]
        rates_all = (rp.ipsi_rate & rp.bilateral_rate & rp.contra_hardly_affected).any()
        sel_ok = (d.ipsi_sel_ratio_600ms >= 0.8) & (d.bilateral_sel_ratio_go < 0.8)
        parts = {"ipsi_rate": rp.ipsi_rate.any(), "bilateral_rate": rp.bilateral_rate.any(), "contra": rp.contra_hardly_affected.any(),
                 "ipsi_sel": (d.ipsi_sel_ratio_600ms >= 0.8).any(), "bilateral_sel": (d.bilateral_sel_ratio_go < 0.8).any()}
        holds = bool(rates_all and sel_ok.any())
        out.append({"trials_rule": rule, "early_lick": early, "pref": pw, "label": lab, **parts,
                    "ipsi_sel_ratio_600ms": f"{d.ipsi_sel_ratio_600ms.min():.2f}-{d.ipsi_sel_ratio_600ms.max():.2f}",
                    "bilateral_sel_ratio_go": f"{d.bilateral_sel_ratio_go.min():.2f}-{d.bilateral_sel_ratio_go.max():.2f}",
                    "outcome_here": "reproduced" if holds else "partially" if any(parts.values()) else "not"})
o2 = pd.DataFrame(out)
print(o2[o2.trials_rule == "per condition"].drop(columns="trials_rule").to_string(index=False))
for rule in ("per condition", "per type"):
    print(f"Outcomes over the method combinations (K, D, L), trials {rule}:", o2[o2.trials_rule == rule].outcome_here.value_counts().to_dict())
s1 = sr[sr.trials_rule == "per condition"]
print("\nN1: ipsilateral selectivity ratio at 600 ms", s1.ipsi_sel_ratio_600ms.min().round(2), "to", s1.ipsi_sel_ratio_600ms.max().round(2),
      "; bilateral selectivity ratio at the go cue", s1.bilateral_sel_ratio_go.min().round(2), "to", s1.bilateral_sel_ratio_go.max().round(2))

Result: partially reproduced. The outcome is the same under all 12 combinations of the method details now required (K1, K2; D1 to D3; L1, L2), with trials per condition. Spike rates recover: 600 ms after offset 8% to 10% of neurons differ from control after ipsilateral photoinhibition, and the population rate is 1.00 to 1.05 of control (1.16 to 1.23 after bilateral photoinhibition). Selectivity after bilateral photoinhibition stays low, 0.22 to 0.33 of control at the go cue. Two parts fail under every combination: ipsilateral selectivity at 600 ms is 0.45 to 0.72 of control, not 0.8 or more; and contralateral photoinhibition changes the rate of 15% to 19% of neurons in some window during or after the light, not fewer than 10%.

Activity space (convention A)¶

The claims on the coding direction use the sessions of the bilateral experiment with more than 5 neurons recorded simultaneously for more than 5 trials per condition (control, ipsilateral, contralateral, bilateral). Here the neurons are putative pyramidal (convention U), observed in every analysis trial, with the training set a random half (H1) or third (H2) of the correct control trials (the claims file's readings). The ipsilateral trials used to build modes 2 and 3 are split with the same fraction. One random split per session (seeded by the session) is used; the spread over 10 seeds is shown as a variant. Answered 2026-10-21: the paper states no selection beyond its rule, so the rule is followed as written, with trials counted per condition (T1) for the outcome and per condition and trial type (T2) as a variant, and the session and neuron counts are reported against the paper's 16 sessions with 6 to 20 neurons (mean 11). Lick-early trials are dropped (K1) or kept (K2), and the outcome must hold under both.

In [30]:
CONDS_A = ["control", "left1", "right1", "bilateral8"]
A = {}
t0 = time.time()
for per_type in (False, True):
    for early in ("drop", "keep"):
        sess = L.a_sessions(U, S, "exp2", CONDS_A, early, per_type)
        for frac, hname in ((0.5, "H1"), (1 / 3, "H2")):
            res = {}
            for sid, uids in sess.items():
                X, t = L.session_counts(U, S, sid, uids, early)
                rng = np.random.default_rng(int(sid.replace("_", "")) % 2 ** 32)
                res[sid] = L.activity_session(X, t, frac, CONDS_A, "left1", rng)
            A[("per type" if per_type else "per condition", early, hname)] = res
print(f"convention A on {len(A)} readings in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

def by_k(df, col, extra=()):
    """Whether `col` holds under some claim reading (H, and `extra`), per lick-early reading, trials per condition (T1)."""
    d = df[df.trials_rule == "per condition"]
    return d.groupby("early_lick")[col].any().to_dict()

cd-stable-over-epochs¶

The direction of the lick right minus lick left difference vector was stable over the sample and delay epochs (correlation 0.61 between late sample and late delay).

Criterion: late sample and late delay are the last 400 ms window of each epoch; Pearson correlation of the two w vectors per session, mean over the sessions; reproduced when within the paper's s.e.m. (0.56 to 0.66). Convention A says that w comes from correct control trials and that cd, the average of w, uses a subset of them; which trials give the w whose correlation is reported is not fixed. Both are run, all correct control trials and the training subset (H1 or H2) that builds cd, and the outcome is the one both give, else methods_underspecified (asked as a question after the first verification round).

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). With w from all correct control trials the mean correlation between late sample and late delay w is 0.563 (lick-early trials dropped) and 0.588 (kept) over 24 sessions, within 0.56 to 0.66. With w from the training subset that builds cd it is 0.534 (H1) or 0.554 (H2) dropped and 0.537 or 0.553 kept, below 0.56. The claims file does not say which trials give w, and the two readings give different outcomes, so the claim is blocked (the first round gave reproduced, from the first reading alone). Counting trials per trial type (T2, a variant) gives 0.559 (dropped) and 0.580 (kept) with all trials. The sessions follow the rule as written (T1, 24 sessions with 6 to 37 neurons, mean 17, against the paper's 16 with 6 to 20, mean 11).

fig3c-cd-recovery-roc¶

Along cd, trajectories recovered after ipsilateral photoinhibition (ROC 0.73 against 0.76 in control) and were little changed by contralateral photoinhibition (0.74), but were permanently altered by bilateral photoinhibition (0.58).

Criterion: convention A; ROC of cd'x between lick right and lick left trials in the last 400 ms of the delay, per session, mean over sessions. Reproduced when all four are within the paper's s.e.m. under H1 or H2; partially when control, ipsilateral and bilateral are and their order holds.

    for c in CONDS_A:

    row["partial"] = row["control_ok"] and row["left1_ok"] and row["bilateral8_ok"] and row["control"] >= row["left1"] > row["bilateral8"]

Result: not reproduced. The bilateral value is within tolerance under every reading (0.558 to 0.559 with trials per condition), but the control ROC is 0.649 to 0.677, below the paper's 0.76 by more than its s.e.m., and the ipsilateral (0.631 to 0.652) and contralateral (0.672 to 0.704) values are also below theirs. The order holds: ipsilateral and contralateral are close to control, and bilateral is lowest. Over 10 random training splits the control mean ranges 0.641 to 0.686. The analysis uses 24 sessions with 6 to 37 neurons, where the paper used 16 with 6 to 20; the answer confirms the rule as written (T1) is the one to follow. The outcome is the same under K1 and K2.

ed8-roc-during-photoinhibition¶

During photoinhibition trajectory separation along cd fell to 0.54 (ipsilateral), 0.64 (contralateral) and 0.54 (bilateral), against 0.72 in control.

Criterion: convention A with cd'x in a window during photoinhibition: (a) the last 400 ms before the ramp, (b) the 400 ms window centred on the photostimulus, (c) the mean over the photostimulus. With 0.8 s of light from delay onset and a 0.2 s ramp, (a) and (b) are the same window (0.2 to 0.6 s after delay onset). Reproduced when all four are within tolerance under a reading.

Result: partially reproduced. During the light, separation along cd falls below control in every condition: control 0.649 to 0.685, ipsilateral 0.49 to 0.58, contralateral 0.59 to 0.64, bilateral 0.48 to 0.55 (trials per condition). Under reading (c) with lick-early trials dropped and H1, the ipsilateral (0.546), contralateral (0.626) and bilateral (0.535) values are within tolerance, but the control value is below 0.70 under every reading, so no reading has all four. With lick-early trials kept at most two are within (ipsilateral 0.534 and contralateral 0.631, window a/b, H1). Under K1 and K2 every perturbed value is below control under every reading, so the effect holds in part under both. The criterion defines no partial outcome; at least half of the four values hold under K1 (three) and K2 (two), so the outcome is partial by the rule given in the Summary.

cd-captures-selectivity¶

Projection on cd captured 65.6% of population selectivity and 36.4% of task-related activity variance over the sample and delay epochs; modes 1 to 5 together captured 98.5% of variance and 95.8% of selectivity.

Criterion: selectivity is the RMS of the trial-averaged lick right minus lick left rate over neurons and time in the sample and delay epochs; variance the RMS of the baseline-subtracted trial-averaged activity; captured fraction (a) RMS ratio or (b) its square; baseline (a) the pre-sample period (the 400 ms window before sample onset), (b) the mean over the trial. Reproduced when the cd values are within tolerance under a reading; the mode 1-5 values must hold for a full reproduction, else partial. Answered 2026-10-21 as not given by the paper: which trials give the trial-averaged activity, (v1) the correct control trials of the training set, from which cd and the modes are built, or (v2) all correct control trials; the outcome must hold under both, and under K1 and K2. Sessions follow convention A's rule (T1).

In [34]:
rows = []
for k, v in A.items():
    for base in ("pre-sample", "trial mean"):
        if base == "pre-sample":
            res = [r for r in v.values() if r["captured"] is not None]
        else:
            res = []
            for sid in v:
                uids = L.a_sessions(U, S, "exp2", CONDS_A, k[1], k[0] == "per type")[sid]
                X, t = L.session_counts(U, S, sid, uids, k[1])
                rng = np.random.default_rng(int(sid.replace("_", "")) % 2 ** 32)
                r_ = L.activity_session(X, t, 0.5 if k[2] == "H1" else 1 / 3, CONDS_A, "left1", rng, baseline="trial mean")
                if r_["captured"] is not None:
                    res.append(r_)
        for vname, key in (("v1 training", "captured"), ("v2 all correct", "captured_v2")):
            cap = pd.DataFrame([r[key] for r in res])
            for ratio in ("RMS", "squared"):
                pw = 1 if ratio == "RMS" else 2
                m = (cap ** pw).mean() * 100
                rows.append({"trials_rule": k[0], "early_lick": k[1], "H": k[2], "trials": vname, "baseline": base, "ratio": ratio,
                             "sessions": len(cap), "sel_cd": m.sel_cd, "var_cd": m.var_cd, "sel_15": m.sel_15, "var_15": m.var_15})

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The answer gives no rule for which trials' average is decomposed, and the claims file now requires the outcome under both readings; they differ. Under v1 (the training trials, the reading run before the answer) cd captures 73.7% to 88.0% of the selectivity with trials per condition, outside 65.6 +/- 5.1 under every reading, so the claim is not reproduced. Under v2 (all correct control trials), with H2, squared ratios and the pre-sample baseline, cd captures 66.2% of the selectivity and 34.6% of the variance with lick-early trials dropped (67.6% and 39.5% kept), both within tolerance, while modes 1 to 5 capture 88.6% to 96.1% of the selectivity and 91.5% to 97.6% of the variance, outside 95.8 +/- 1.2 and 98.5 +/- 0.5, so v2 is partial. Under H1, v2 gives 74.4% or more of the selectivity. The captured fractions are measured on trial averages that include the trials used to build cd and the modes (all of them under v1, part of them under v2), so they are in-sample; the claims file names no held-out reading, and none is run.

fig3c-cd-predicts-movement and fig4-bilateral-cd-predicts-movement¶

Activity along cd predicts the upcoming movement trial by trial; deviations toward the lick right trajectory predict more lick right responses, and vice versa. (fig3c)

Even after bilateral photoinhibition destroys average selectivity, single-trial activity along cd predicts the upcoming movement. (fig4)

Criterion: for each session the decision boundary on the training control trials; for each held-out control and perturbation trial the distance of cd'x from the boundary in the last 400 ms before the go cue; trials pooled over sessions. Reproduced, for control and ipsilateral trials (fig3c) or for bilateral trials (fig4), when the fraction of trials whose lick falls on the side of the boundary is above 0.5 by a one-sided binomial test at p < 0.05, and lick right performance rises and lick left performance falls with distance (Spearman correlation over bins of 4 of the right sign). Bins hold at least one trial; bins with at least 5 trials are shown as a variant.

def predicts(trials, cond, min_bin=1):
    d = trials[trials.cond == cond]
    pred = (d.d > 0) == d.licked_right
    k, n = int(pred.sum()), len(d)
    pb = stats.binomtest(k, n, 0.5, alternative="greater").pvalue
    d = d.assign(bin=np.floor(d.d / 4) * 4 + 2)
    out = {"n": n, "frac_pred": k / n, "binom_p": pb}
    for side, name in ((True, "right"), (False, "left")):
        g = d[d.right == side].groupby("bin").hit.agg(["mean", "size"])
        g = g[g["size"] >= min_bin]
        rho = stats.spearmanr(g.index, g["mean"]) if len(g) > 2 else None
        out[f"rho_{name}"] = rho.statistic if rho else np.nan; out[f"p_{name}"] = rho.pvalue if rho else np.nan
        out[f"bins_{name}"] = len(g)
    out["holds"] = (pb < 0.05) and out["rho_right"] > 0 and out["rho_left"] < 0
    return out

Result: fig3c-cd-predicts-movement reproduced; fig4-bilateral-cd-predicts-movement reproduced. The side of the decision boundary predicts the lick in 67% to 69% of held-out control trials (1890 to 2895 trials) and 63% to 68% of ipsilateral trials (261 to 448), and in 59% to 64% of bilateral trials (777 to 1139); every binomial p is below 1e-6. Lick right performance rises with the distance from the boundary (Spearman rho +0.28 to +0.99 for control and ipsilateral trials, +0.84 to +1.00 for bilateral ones), and lick left performance falls (rho -0.76 to -1.00), under every reading, with bins of at least one or at least 5 trials. Both hold under K1 and K2 with the rule as written (T1), as the answers require.

fig3d-persistent-mode and fig3e-ramping-mode¶

A persistent mode, built to capture the sustained effect of ipsilateral perturbation, stays altered past movement onset but neither discriminates trial type nor predicts behaviour on control trials. (fig3d)

A ramping mode capturing most remaining variance shows non-selective ramping in the delay epoch, does not predict behaviour, and is resistant to unilateral and bilateral perturbation. (fig3e)

Criteria: mode 2 is the difference of mean response vectors, ipsilateral perturbed minus control lick right correct trials, at the go cue; mode 4 the first SVD eigenvector of the baseline-subtracted PSTH matrix (sample and delay epochs) made orthogonal to modes 1 to 3. fig3d is reproduced when the session mean ROC between lick right and lick left control trials is within 2 bootstrap s.e.m. of 0.5, the fraction predicted is not above 0.5 by the one-sided binomial test, and the ipsilateral minus control difference at the go cue is outside 2 s.e.m. of zero. fig3e is reproduced when the control projection rises over the delay (positive in the session mean), its ROC and fraction predicted fail the tests of fig3d, and the perturbed minus control difference at the go cue is within 2 bootstrap s.e.m. of zero for ipsilateral, contralateral and bilateral trials. Answered 2026-10-21: the ipsilateral trials that build modes 2 and 3 are split like the control trials, so projected ipsilateral trials are ones not used to build them, as done here. The sign of mode 4 is not given; readings (g1) the mode oriented to a positive weight sum, ramping judged by a positive change over the delay; (g2) each session's mode oriented so that the control projection at the go cue exceeds that at delay onset, ramping judged by the size of the change against 2 bootstrap s.e.m., with ROC and the go-cue differences following the orientation. The outcome must hold under both, and under K1 and K2 (T1). The bootstrap is over sessions (1000 resamples).

In [36]:
def boot_sem(x, n=1000, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed); x = np.asarray(x, float)
    return np.std([rng.choice(x, len(x)).mean() for _ in range(n)])
rows = []
for k, v0 in A.items():
    v = {sid: r for sid, r in v0.items() if r["m2"] is not None}
    for mode in ("m2", "m4"):
        roc = np.array([r[mode]["roc"] for r in v.values()])
        k_ok = sum(r[mode]["n_correct_pred"] for r in v.values()); n_all = sum(r[mode]["n_pred"] for r in v.values())
        row = {"trials_rule": k[0], "early_lick": k[1], "H": k[2], "mode": mode, "sessions": len(v), "dropped": len(v0) - len(v),
               "roc": roc.mean(), "roc_2sem": 2 * boot_sem(roc),
               "frac_pred": k_ok / n_all, "binom_p": stats.binomtest(k_ok, n_all, 0.5, alternative="greater").pvalue}
        row["roc_near_half"] = abs(row["roc"] - 0.5) <= row["roc_2sem"]
        for c in ("left1", "right1", "bilateral8"):
            dg = np.array([r[mode]["diff_go"][c] for r in v.values()])
            row[f"diff_{c}"] = dg.mean(); row[f"diff_{c}_2sem"] = 2 * boot_sem(dg)
        rise = np.array([r[mode]["rise_delay"] for r in v.values()])
        row["rise_delay"] = rise.mean(); row["rise_2sem"] = 2 * boot_sem(rise)
        rows.append(row)
md = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(md.round(3).to_string(index=False))
m2 = md[md["mode"] == "m2"].copy()
m2["holds_3d"] = m2.roc_near_half & (m2.binom_p >= 0.05) & (m2.diff_left1.abs() > m2.diff_left1_2sem)
m4 = md[md["mode"] == "m4"].copy()
m4["holds_3e"] = (m4.rise_delay > 0) & m4.roc_near_half & (m4.binom_p >= 0.05) & \
    np.all([m4[f"diff_{c}"].abs() <= m4[f"diff_{c}_2sem"] for c in ("left1", "right1", "bilateral8")], axis=0)
print("\nfig3d:"); print(m2[["trials_rule", "early_lick", "H", "roc", "roc_2sem", "frac_pred", "binom_p", "diff_left1", "diff_left1_2sem", "holds_3d"]].round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nfig3e:"); print(m4[["trials_rule", "early_lick", "H", "rise_delay", "rise_2sem", "roc", "roc_2sem", "frac_pred", "binom_p",
                           "diff_left1", "diff_left1_2sem", "diff_right1", "diff_right1_2sem", "diff_bilateral8", "diff_bilateral8_2sem", "holds_3e"]].round(3).to_string(index=False))
# Reading g2 for mode 4: per session, the mode oriented so that the control projection rises from delay onset to the go
# cue; ramping judged by the size of that change against 2 bootstrap s.e.m. ROC, the go-cue differences and the
# predictions follow the orientation (ROC becomes 1 - ROC and differences change sign where the mode is flipped; the
# fraction predicted does not depend on the sign).
rows = []
for k, v0 in A.items():
    v = {sid: r for sid, r in v0.items() if r["m4"] is not None}
    sgn = np.array([1.0 if r["m4"]["rise_delay"] >= 0 else -1.0 for r in v.values()])
    rise = np.array([abs(r["m4"]["rise_delay"]) for r in v.values()])
    roc = np.array([r["m4"]["roc"] if s > 0 else 1 - r["m4"]["roc"] for s, r in zip(sgn, v.values())])
    row = {"trials_rule": k[0], "early_lick": k[1], "H": k[2], "sessions": len(v), "flipped": int((sgn < 0).sum()),
           "rise_delay": rise.mean(), "rise_2sem": 2 * boot_sem(rise), "roc": roc.mean(), "roc_2sem": 2 * boot_sem(roc)}
    for c in ("left1", "right1", "bilateral8"):
        dg = sgn * np.array([r["m4"]["diff_go"][c] for r in v.values()])
        row[f"diff_{c}"] = dg.mean(); row[f"diff_{c}_2sem"] = 2 * boot_sem(dg)
    row["frac_pred"] = m4.set_index(["trials_rule", "early_lick", "H"]).loc[k, "frac_pred"]
    row["binom_p"] = m4.set_index(["trials_rule", "early_lick", "H"]).loc[k, "binom_p"]
    rows.append(row)
m4g2 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
m4g2["ramps"] = m4g2.rise_delay > m4g2.rise_2sem
m4g2["roc_near_half"] = (m4g2.roc - 0.5).abs() <= m4g2.roc_2sem
m4g2["holds_3e"] = m4g2.ramps & m4g2.roc_near_half & (m4g2.binom_p >= 0.05) & \
    np.all([m4g2[f"diff_{c}"].abs() <= m4g2[f"diff_{c}_2sem"] for c in ("left1", "right1", "bilateral8")], axis=0)
print("\nfig3e, reading g2:"); print(m4g2.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nT1, per K reading: fig3d holds", by_k(m2, "holds_3d"), "; fig3e holds under g1", by_k(m4, "holds_3e"), "and under g2", by_k(m4g2, "holds_3e"))
print("fig3e parts, T1: predicts above chance (binomial p < 0.05) under every reading",
      bool((m4[m4.trials_rule == "per condition"].binom_p < 0.05).all()), "; g1 rise positive", by_k(m4.assign(r=m4.rise_delay > 0), "r"),
      "; g2 ramps beyond 2 s.e.m.", by_k(m4g2, "ramps"))


# Per-session ROC of modes 2 and 4 on held-out control trials (verifier's request), T1, with |ROC - 0.5|.
# Mode 4 is shown as oriented by g1 (positive weight sum); under g2 a flipped session has 1 - ROC, and
# |ROC - 0.5| is the same.
ps = []
for k, v0 in A.items():
    if k[0] != "per condition":
        continue
    for sid, r in v0.items():
        if r["m2"] is None:
            continue
        ps.append({"early_lick": k[1], "H": k[2], "sid": sid, "neurons": r["n_neurons"], "roc_m2": r["m2"]["roc"], "roc_m4": r["m4"]["roc"]})
ps = pd.DataFrame(ps)
ps["abs_m2"] = (ps.roc_m2 - 0.5).abs(); ps["abs_m4"] = (ps.roc_m4 - 0.5).abs()
print(ps.pivot(index="sid", columns=["early_lick", "H"], values=["roc_m2", "roc_m4"]).round(3).to_string())
print("\nMean |ROC - 0.5| over sessions, with 2 bootstrap s.e.m.; for reference the cd ROC at the go cue on the same sessions:")
for (e_, h_), d in ps.groupby(["early_lick", "H"]):
    cd_roc = np.array([r["roc_go"]["control"] for s_, r in A[("per condition", e_, h_)].items() if s_ in set(d.sid)])
    print(f"  {e_}, {h_}: mode 2 {d.abs_m2.mean():.3f} (2 s.e.m. {2 * boot_sem(d.abs_m2):.3f}); mode 4 {d.abs_m4.mean():.3f} "
          f"(2 s.e.m. {2 * boot_sem(d.abs_m4):.3f}); cd |ROC - 0.5| {np.mean(np.abs(cd_roc - 0.5)):.3f}; sessions {len(d)}")

Result: fig3d-persistent-mode not reproduced; fig3e-ramping-mode not reproduced. The answer confirmed the split of the ipsilateral trials used here, and both outcomes are the same under K1 and K2, and for fig3e under g1 and g2. The persistent mode is altered by ipsilateral photoinhibition up to the go cue (difference 1.08 to 1.75, more than its 2 s.e.m. of 0.57 to 0.66), but it predicts the lick on control trials above chance (59% to 62% of trials, binomial p below 1e-6) under every reading, and under two of four readings with trials per condition its ROC (0.408, 0.430) is further than 2 s.e.m. from 0.5. The ramping mode is resistant to all three perturbations under the rule as written (T1): the differences are within 2 s.e.m. under every reading and either orientation. Under the T2 variant with lick-early trials dropped, H1 and g1, the ipsilateral difference (-0.353) is beyond its 2 s.e.m. (0.294). Under g1 its change over the delay is -0.73 to +0.11, positive under one of four readings, and its ROC is near 0.5 under three of four; under g2 the change is 1.26 to 1.56 against 2 s.e.m. of 0.47 to 0.53, so it ramps, and its ROC is near 0.5 under all four. Under both it predicts the lick in 55% to 58% of control trials, above chance (p below 1e-6), so it fails the claim.

Per session (T1), the mean of |ROC - 0.5| on held-out control trials is 0.091 to 0.127 for the persistent mode and 0.064 to 0.103 for the ramping mode, against 0.154 to 0.181 for cd on the same sessions. A session-mean ROC near 0.5 therefore partly reflects separation of opposite sign in different sessions; the binomial test of the fraction predicted, which does not depend on the sign, fails both claims under every reading.

ed6b-session-bias-predicted¶

In each session the behavioural bias after bilateral photoinhibition followed the side of the control trajectory that the perturbed cd trajectory ended closer to.

Criterion: per session with bilateral photoinhibition, the mean cd'x of bilateral trials at the go cue relative to the decision boundary (convention A), and the behavioural bias of ed6a-bilateral-inconsistent-bias; reproduced when the signs agree in a majority of sessions, above chance by a one-sided binomial test at p < 0.05.
