The side of the boundary at which the bilateral trials end agrees in sign with the behavioural bias in 11 to 15 of 19 to 24 sessions, not above chance (one-sided binomial p 0.15 to 0.50) under any reading. The legend's five example sessions are not identified here. With the rule as written (T1) it is 13 to 15 of 24 sessions (p 0.15 to 0.42), not above chance under K1 or K2, so the answers leave the outcome unchanged.

ed9f-reaction-time¶

Reaction times were faster on trials whose cd trajectory was far from the decision boundary at the go cue.

Criterion: convention A; reaction time is the first lick after the go cue, relative to the session mean; distance is the absolute distance of cd'x from the boundary at the go cue; lick right and lick left trials pooled; readings (a) control trials, (b) all trials. Reproduced when the Spearman correlation between distance and reaction time is negative with p < 0.05. Answered 2026-10-21: the paper does not say how a lick is detected; the files hold no lick times, only lick_trace, an analogue signal ("the animal's tongue movement when licking") in 5 s chunks at 10 kHz. The outcome stands only if it is the same over the thresholds tried, else methods_underspecified. The thresholds tried here, all choices over a range: the raw signal rising above 0.10, 0.12 or 0.14 (level), above the pre-go baseline mean plus 0.01, 0.02 or 0.05 (rise), and above the baseline mean plus 3, 5, 10 or 20 baseline standard deviations (sd). The baseline is the 300 ms before the go cue, and the lick is searched up to 1.4 s after it (the chunk ends 1.43 s after the go cue in most trials). Projected trials are the held-out trials of convention A; a trial without a detected lick under a rule leaves that rule's test.

t0 = time.time()
RULES = {"level 0.10": ("level", 0.10), "level 0.12": ("level", 0.12), "level 0.14": ("level", 0.14),
         "level 0.16": ("level", 0.16), "level 0.20": ("level", 0.20), "level 0.25": ("level", 0.25),
         "rise 0.01": ("rise", 0.01), "rise 0.02": ("rise", 0.02), "rise 0.05": ("rise", 0.05),
         "sd 3": ("sd", 3), "sd 5": ("sd", 5), "sd 10": ("sd", 10), "sd 20": ("sd", 20)}
LK, lk_rows = {}, []
for sid in sorted(set().union(*[set(v) for v in A.values()])):
    s = S[sid]; tr = s["trials"]
    aid = assets[assets.path == s["path"]].asset_id.iloc[0]
    df, info = L.lick_onsets(aid, tr.go.values, RULES)
    df["go"] = tr.go.values; df["outcome"] = tr.outcome.values; df["early_lick"] = tr.early_lick.values
    LK[sid] = df
    h = df[df.read & (df.outcome == "hit") & ~df.early_lick]
    lk_rows.append({"sid": sid, "chunks": info["chunks"], "nonuniform_chunks": info["chunks_nonuniform"],
                    "behaving": int(tr.behaving.sum()), "read": int((df.read & tr.behaving.values).sum()),
                    "baseline": h.baseline.median(), "max_after_go": h.max_after.median(),
                    **{f"hit_detected_{r}": (h[r].notna().mean() if len(h) else np.nan) for r in ("level 0.12", "rise 0.02", "sd 5", "sd 20")},
                    "median_rt_ms_sd5": h["sd 5"].median() * 1000})
lk = pd.DataFrame(lk_rows)
print(f"lick_trace windows read for {len(lk)} sessions in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
print(lk.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nSessions where a lick is detected (sd 5) on more than half of correct trials without an early lick:",
      int((lk["hit_detected_sd 5"] > 0.5).sum()), "of", len(lk))

# Does the trace carry licks? Detection on correct trials (the mouse licked) against no-response trials (it did not),
# pooled over the sessions, and the same for the first session (by id) of each other group of the dandiset.
def lick_contrast(df):
    ok = df.read & ~df.early_lick
    h, n = df[ok & (df.outcome == "hit")], df[ok & (df.outcome == "ignore")]
    return {"hit_trials": len(h), "no_response_trials": len(n), "max_minus_baseline_hit_median": (h.max_after - h.baseline).median(),
            **{f"{r}": f"{h[r].notna().mean():.2f}/{n[r].notna().mean() if len(n) else np.nan:.2f}" for r in RULES}}
print("\nFraction of trials with a detected lick, correct / no-response (trials without an early lick):")
print("convention A sessions:", lick_contrast(pd.concat(LK.values(), ignore_index=True)))
ref = []
for exp in ("exp1", "exp3", "no_photostim_record"):
    sid = sorted(k for k, s_ in S.items() if s_["exp"] == exp and s_["trials"].behaving.any())[0]
    tr = S[sid]["trials"]
    df, _ = L.lick_onsets(assets[assets.path == S[sid]["path"]].asset_id.iloc[0], tr.go.values, RULES)
    df["outcome"] = tr.outcome.values; df["early_lick"] = tr.early_lick.values
    ref.append({"group": exp, "sid": sid, **lick_contrast(df)})
print(pd.DataFrame(ref).round(4).to_string(index=False))

rows = []
for k, v in A.items():
    tt = []
    for sid, r in v.items():
        tb = r["trials"].merge(LK[sid].drop(columns=["outcome", "early_lick"]), on="go", how="left")
        tb["sid"] = sid
        tt.append(tb)
    tt = pd.concat(tt, ignore_index=True)
    for reading, sel in (("a control", tt.cond == "control"), ("b all", tt.cond.notna())):
        for rule in RULES:
            d = tt[sel & tt[rule].notna()].copy()
            d["rt_rel"] = d[rule] - d.groupby("sid")[rule].transform("mean")
            rho = stats.spearmanr(d.d.abs(), d.rt_rel) if len(d) > 2 else None
            rows.append({"trials_rule": k[0], "early_lick": k[1], "H": k[2], "trials": reading, "rule": rule,
                         "n": len(d), "sessions": d.sid.nunique(), "median_rt_ms": d[rule].median() * 1000,
                         "rho": rho.statistic if rho else np.nan, "p": rho.pvalue if rho else np.nan})
rt = pd.DataFrame(rows)
rt["holds"] = (rt.rho < 0) & (rt.p < 0.05)
print(rt[rt.trials_rule == "per condition"].round(4).to_string(index=False))
j9 = rt[rt.trials_rule == "per condition"].groupby(["early_lick", "rule"]).holds.any().unstack(0)
print("\nT1: holds under some reading (a or b, H1 or H2), per threshold and K reading:")
print(j9.to_string())
print("Thresholds and K readings under which it holds:", int(j9.values.sum()), "of", j9.size)
print("T2 (variant):", rt[rt.trials_rule == "per type"].groupby("early_lick").holds.mean().round(2).to_dict(), "fraction of rows holding")
print("rho range, T1:", rt[rt.trials_rule == "per condition"].rho.min().round(3), "to", rt[rt.trials_rule == "per condition"].rho.max().round(3))

# Raw lick_trace (verifier's request): per session, the pre-go baseline and the rise after the go cue
# on correct and on no-response trials, for every convention A session (experiment 2) and the
# reference sessions; then example windows of four correct trials from two experiment-2 and two
# experiment-3 sessions.
def trace_summary(df, sid, group):
    ok = df.read & ~df.early_lick
    h, n = df[ok & (df.outcome == "hit")], df[ok & (df.outcome == "ignore")]
    r = {"group": group, "sid": sid, "hit": len(h), "no_response": len(n), "baseline_median": h.baseline.median(),
         "baseline_sd_median": h.baseline_sd.median()}
    for name, d in (("hit", h), ("noresp", n)):
        rise = d.max_after - d.baseline
        r[f"rise_{name}_q50_q90_q99"] = "/".join(f"{x:.4f}" for x in rise.quantile([0.5, 0.9, 0.99])) if len(d) else ""
    return r
ex3 = sorted(k for k, s_ in S.items() if s_["exp"] == "exp3" and s_["trials"].behaving.any())
LK3 = {}
for sid in ex3:
    tr = S[sid]["trials"]
    df, _ = L.lick_onsets(assets[assets.path == S[sid]["path"]].asset_id.iloc[0], tr.go.values, RULES)
    df["go"] = tr.go.values; df["outcome"] = tr.outcome.values; df["early_lick"] = tr.early_lick.values
    LK3[sid] = df
summ_rows = [trace_summary(df, sid, "exp2 (convention A)") for sid, df in LK.items()] + [trace_summary(df, sid, "exp3") for sid, df in LK3.items()]
print(pd.DataFrame(summ_rows).round(4).to_string(index=False))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(14, 2.6), sharey=False)
tt_ = np.arange(-0.3, 1.4, 1e-4)[:17000]
for ax, sid in zip(axes, sorted(LK)[:2] + ex3[:2]):
    tr = S[sid]["trials"]
    g = tr[(tr.outcome == "hit") & ~tr.early_lick & tr.behaving].go.values[:4]
    ws = L.lick_windows(assets[assets.path == S[sid]["path"]].asset_id.iloc[0], g)
    for k_, w_ in enumerate(ws):
        if w_ is None:
            continue
        ax.plot(tt_[:len(w_)], w_, lw=0.6)
        print(f"{sid} ({S[sid]['exp']}), correct trial {k_}: baseline {w_[:3000].mean():.4f}, min {w_.min():.4f}, max {w_.max():.4f},"
              f" max after go minus baseline {w_[3000:].max() - w_[:3000].mean():.4f}")
    ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.5); ax.set_title(f"{sid} ({S[sid]['exp']})", fontsize=8); ax.set_xlabel("s from go cue")
axes[0].set_ylabel("lick_trace (a.u.)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# Variant (verifier's suggestion; reference only, the claim's sessions are those of experiment 2):
# the same test on experiment 3, whose lick trace carries licks. Convention A on the experiment-3
# sessions (more than 5 neurons with more than 5 trials in each of control, left4, right4 and
# bilateral2), cd and boundary as for ed7e, reaction time from the trace under every rule.
rows = []
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    sess3 = L.a_sessions(U, S, "exp3", ["control", "left4", "right4", "bilateral2"], early, False)
    for frac, hname in ((0.5, "H1"), (1 / 3, "H2")):
        tt = []
        for sid, uids in sess3.items():
            X, t = L.session_counts(U, S, sid, uids, early)
            r = L.activity_session(X, t, frac, ["control", "left4", "right4", "bilateral2"], "left4", np.random.default_rng(int(sid.replace("_", "")) % 2 ** 32))
            tb = r["trials"].merge(LK3[sid].drop(columns=["outcome", "early_lick"]), on="go", how="left"); tb["sid"] = sid
            tt.append(tb)
        tt = pd.concat(tt, ignore_index=True)
        for reading, sel in (("a control", tt.cond == "control"), ("b all", tt.cond.notna())):
            for rule in RULES:
                d = tt[sel & tt[rule].notna()].copy()
                d["rt_rel"] = d[rule] - d.groupby("sid")[rule].transform("mean")
                rho = stats.spearmanr(d.d.abs(), d.rt_rel) if len(d) > 2 else None
                rows.append({"early_lick": early, "H": hname, "trials": reading, "rule": rule, "sessions": d.sid.nunique(), "n": len(d),
                             "median_rt_ms": d[rule].median() * 1000, "rho": rho.statistic if rho else np.nan, "p": rho.pvalue if rho else np.nan})
rt3 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
rt3["holds"] = (rt3.rho < 0) & (rt3.p < 0.05)
print(rt3.round(4).to_string(index=False))
j3 = rt3.groupby(["early_lick", "rule"]).holds.any().unstack(0)
print("\nExperiment 3: holds under some reading (a or b, H1 or H2), per threshold and K reading:")
print(j3.to_string())
print("Thresholds and K readings under which it holds:", int(j3.values.sum()), "of", j3.size, "; rho range", rt3.rho.min().round(3), "to", rt3.rho.max().round(3))

Result: blocked (data_missing). The answer let the claim be tested over a range of lick thresholds, and the test shows that the lick trace of these sessions holds no licks. In the 24 experiment-2 sessions of convention A the trace sits at a baseline of 0.166 to 0.193 and its median rise after the go cue on correct trials, where the mouse licked, is 0.0013 to 0.0022 per session (99th percentile at most 0.0159), the same as on no-response trials (0.0013 to 0.0021); the example traces show the same. After the first verification round, raw levels of 0.16, 0.20 and 0.25 were added, since the levels 0.10 to 0.14 lie below the baseline of these sessions. Pooled over 3660 correct and 61 no-response trials, no rule finds a lick on correct trials more often than on no-response trials (level 0.16, 0.37 against 0.56; 3 s.d., 0.59 against 0.38; level 0.14, 0.05 against 0.03; every other rule 0.02 or less), and no session has a lick detected (5 s.d.) on more than half of its correct trials. The correlation holds under 5 of the 26 combinations of threshold and lick-early reading, on 3 to 10 trials, so by the claims file's rule the outcome would also be methods_underspecified. In experiment 3 the trace carries licks: the median rise on correct trials is 0.0385 to 0.0717 per session, against 0.0017 to 0.0213 on no-response trials. As a variant on those 6 sessions (a different experiment from the claim's), the correlation is negative with p < 0.05 under 18 of the 26 combinations; it fails for the levels that lie near or above the trace (0.10, 0.20, 0.25) and for a rise of 0.05, and its rho ranges from -0.256 to 0.172. The lick times the claim needs are not in the dandiset for the claim's sessions.

ed9c-cd-window-robust¶

The recovery along cd after unilateral perturbation does not depend on the window used to compute cd (first or last 400 ms of the delay epoch).

Criterion: as fig3c-cd-recovery-roc with cd from the first or the last 400 ms of the delay epoch; reproduced when, for both windows, the ipsilateral ROC at the end of the delay is within 0.05 of the control ROC and the bilateral ROC is lower than the ipsilateral. A 400 ms window inside a 400 ms period is a single window, so cd is w of that window.

        for frac, hname in ((0.5, "H1"), (1 / 3, "H2")):

                    X, t = L.session_counts(U, S, sid, uids, early)
                    rng = np.random.default_rng(int(sid.replace("_", "")) % 2 ** 32)
                    roc.append(L.activity_session(X, t, frac, CONDS_A, "left1", rng, cd_window=win)["roc_go"])

Result: reproduced. With cd from the first or the last 400 ms of the delay, the ipsilateral ROC is within 0.05 of the control ROC and the bilateral ROC is below the ipsilateral one under H1 and H2 with lick-early trials dropped, and under H2 with them kept (under H1 kept, the ipsilateral ROC with the first window is 0.059 to 0.072 below control). The criterion allows either H reading, so the claim holds under both lick-early readings, as the answer on K requires, with the rule as written (T1).

ed7e-roc-larger-photoinhibition¶

Trajectory separation along cd at the end of the delay was 0.80 in control, 0.64 after ipsilateral and 0.68 after contralateral four-spot photoinhibition, and 0.54 after bilateral one-spot photoinhibition.

Criterion: convention A on experiment 3 sessions with more than 5 simultaneously recorded neurons tested on more than 3 trials per condition (control, ipsilateral four spots, contralateral four spots, bilateral one spot per side). Tolerances are the legend's s.e.m. (the bilateral 0.8 read as 0.08). Reproduced when all four are within tolerance under H1 or H2.

In [43]:
CONDS_7 = ["control", "left4", "right4", "bilateral2"]
EXP7E = {"control": (0.80, 0.08), "left4": (0.64, 0.10), "right4": (0.68, 0.15), "bilateral2": (0.54, 0.08)}
rows, A7 = [], {}
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    sess = L.a_sessions(U, S, "exp3", CONDS_7, early, False, min_trials=3)
    for frac, hname in ((0.5, "H1"), (1 / 3, "H2")):
        res = {}
        for sid, uids in sess.items():
            X, t = L.session_counts(U, S, sid, uids, early)
            res[sid] = L.activity_session(X, t, frac, CONDS_7, "left4", np.random.default_rng(int(sid.replace("_", "")) % 2 ** 32))
        A7[(early, hname)] = res
        roc = pd.DataFrame([r["roc_go"] for r in res.values()])
        row = {"early_lick": early, "H": hname, "sessions": len(roc), "mice": len({s.split('_')[0] for s in res}),
               "neurons": f"{min(r['n_neurons'] for r in res.values())}-{max(r['n_neurons'] for r in res.values())}"}
        for c in CONDS_7:
            row[c] = roc[c].mean(); row[c + "_sem"] = roc[c].sem(); row[c + "_ok"] = abs(roc[c].mean() - EXP7E[c][0]) <= EXP7E[c][1]
        row["all_four"] = all(row[c + "_ok"] for c in CONDS_7)
        rows.append(row)
r7e = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(r7e.round(3).to_string(index=False))

Result: partially reproduced. The answer on lick-early trials requires the outcome under K1 and K2, and it is partial under both. Over 6 sessions of 3 mice (6 to 23 neurons), the ipsilateral (0.60 to 0.67) and contralateral (0.69 to 0.71) four-spot values are within tolerance, and the bilateral one-spot value (0.615 to 0.616) is within it with lick-early trials dropped (0.646 to 0.665 kept, outside). The control ROC (0.680 to 0.689) is below the paper's 0.80 by more than its s.e.m., so no reading has all four; bilateral separation is lower than ipsilateral only under K1 with H2 (0.616 against 0.672). The criterion defines no partial outcome; three of the four values hold under K1 and two under K2, so the outcome is partial by the rule given in the Summary.

ed7-larger-photoinhibition¶

Bilateral photoinhibition with one spot per side changed selectivity more persistently than unilateral photoinhibition with four spots; selectivity recovered to 80% of control 490 ms after ipsilateral and 235 ms after contralateral four-spot photoinhibition, and did not recover after bilateral one-spot photoinhibition; recovery after unilateral photoinhibition was less robust with larger photoinhibition.

Criterion: convention D on experiment 3. Reproduced when both times are within tolerance, bilateral one-spot selectivity stays below 80% of control at the end of the delay, and the selectivity change at the go cue is larger (more negative) after bilateral one-spot than after ipsilateral four-spot photoinhibition; "less robust with size" is judged by the ipsilateral four-spot ROC at the end of the delay (ed7e) lower than the ipsilateral one-spot ROC (fig3c), by sign. The method details answered 2026-10-21 (K, D, L, E) are run as for fig1g, and the outcome must be the same under all; trials are counted per condition (N1).

In [44]:
OFF3 = {"left4": -0.9, "right4": -0.9, "bilateral2": -0.9}
e3 = U[(U.exp == "exp3") & (U.cls == "pyr")]
rec3, courses3 = {}, {}
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    rec3[early], courses3[early] = L.recovery_readings(e3, S, OFF3, SEL[early], early, no_recovery=("bilateral2",), per_types=(False,))
rec3 = pd.concat(rec3.values(), ignore_index=True).rename(columns={"early": "early_lick"})
dsel = []
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for key, (tl, cm) in courses3[early].items():
        jgo = int(np.argmin(abs(tl - 0.0)))
        dsel.append({"early_lick": early, "bin": key[0], "pref": key[1], "S": key[3], "label": key[4],
                     "dsel_go_bilateral2": cm["bilateral2"][jgo] - cm["control"][jgo], "dsel_go_left4": cm["left4"][jgo] - cm["control"][jgo]})
rec3 = rec3.merge(pd.DataFrame(dsel), on=["early_lick", "bin", "pref", "S", "label"])
rec3["ipsi_ok"] = (rec3.left4 - 490).abs() <= 280
rec3["contra_ok"] = (rec3.right4 - 235).abs() <= 156
rec3["n_ok"] = (rec3.n - 40).abs() <= 4
rec3["bil_no_recovery"] = ~rec3.bilateral2_recovers_by_go
rec3["bil_larger_change"] = rec3.dsel_go_bilateral2 < rec3.dsel_go_left4
rec3["holds_D"] = rec3.ipsi_ok & rec3.contra_ok & rec3.bil_no_recovery & rec3.bil_larger_change
print(rec3[["early_lick", "pref", "label", "search", "bin", "S", "n", "left4", "left4_boot", "left4_sd", "right4", "right4_boot", "right4_sd",
            "bilateral2", "bilateral2_max_ratio_to_go", "dsel_go_bilateral2", "dsel_go_left4", "holds_D"]].round(2).to_string(index=False))
roc_cmp = []
for early in ("drop", "keep"):
    for h in ("H1", "H2"):
        r4 = r7e[(r7e.early_lick == early) & (r7e.H == h)].left4.iloc[0]
        r1 = r3c[(r3c.trials_rule == "per condition") & (r3c.early_lick == early) & (r3c.H == h)].left1.iloc[0]
        roc_cmp.append({"early_lick": early, "H": h, "roc_ipsi_4_spots": r4, "roc_ipsi_1_spot": r1, "less_robust": r4 < r1})
roc_cmp = pd.DataFrame(roc_cmp)
print("\n", roc_cmp.round(3).to_string(index=False))
s7 = rec3.groupby(["early_lick", "pref", "label", "search"]).agg(
    sum=("holds_D", "sum"), size=("holds_D", "size"), left4_ms=("left4", lambda x: f"{x.min():.0f}-{x.max():.0f}"),
    right4_ms=("right4", lambda x: f"{x.min():.0f}-{x.max():.0f}"), ipsi_ok=("ipsi_ok", "sum"), contra_ok=("contra_ok", "sum"),
    bil_no_recovery=("bil_no_recovery", "sum"), bil_larger_change=("bil_larger_change", "sum")).reset_index()
s7 = s7.merge(roc_cmp.groupby("early_lick").less_robust.any().reset_index(), on="early_lick")
s7["holds"] = (s7["sum"] > 0) & s7.less_robust
s7["outcome_here"] = np.where(s7.holds, "reproduced", "not")
print("\n", s7.to_string(index=False))
print("Outcomes over the method combinations (K, D, L, E):", s7.outcome_here.value_counts().to_dict())
print("Included neurons:", rec3.n.min(), "to", rec3.n.max(), "; paper 40 (tolerance 4)")

Outcomes over the method combinations (K, D, L, E): {'not': 14, 'reproduced': 10}
Included neurons: 58 to 62 ; paper 40 (tolerance 4)

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The answer gives neither the window label nor the other details, and the claims file now requires one outcome over all of them (K1, K2; D1 to D3; L1, L2; E1, E2); they differ. 10 of the 24 combinations have readings that hold, all with centre labels (L1), and 14 have none, among them every combination with end labels (L2). With lick-early trials dropped and centre labels the ipsilateral four-spot recovery is 650 to 700 ms (paper 490 +/- 280) and the contralateral one 50 to 350 ms (235 +/- 156); the selectivity change at the go cue is -0.38 to -0.49 after bilateral one-spot and -0.10 to +0.14 after ipsilateral four-spot photoinhibition. With end labels the ipsilateral time is 750 ms or more; 750 ms is inside the tolerance (210 to 770 ms), and the ipsilateral time holds in 8 of 16 readings for lick-early trials dropped with D2 or D3 and end labels, but these combinations fail on the other parts. With the preference set per bin (D3), bilateral selectivity reaches up to 0.87 of control before the go cue in half the readings. The end of the search (E1, E2) does not change which combinations hold. The four-spot ipsilateral ROC is below the one-spot ROC under H1 (0.607 against 0.652 with lick-early trials dropped, 0.604 against 0.631 kept). 58 to 62 neurons are included, against the paper's 40. With lick-early trials kept, 1% to 4% of the experiment-3 photoinhibition trials have their light before its logged time (data check).

ed1-monolithic-models-fail¶

Monolithic network models (integrator, integrator with corrective feedback, trained random recurrent networks) do not recover the unperturbed trajectory after transient silencing of half their neurons.

Criterion: simulations with the parameters of the Methods and the Extended Data Fig. 1 legend (simple integrator N = 100, tau 100 ms, one eigenvalue 0.99; FORCE network N = 400, tau 200 ms, tanh, p = 0.1, gain 1.5, 30 iterations; silencing 0.2 to 1.0 s of 2 s); 1 ms step, fixed seeds, at least 10 networks. Reproduced when, at 2 s, the output of each model differs from its unperturbed output by more than 10% of the unperturbed selectivity, for the simple integrator and the transient-input FORCE network. The FORCE target (a ramp to plus or minus 1 at 2 s), the feedback weights (uniform from -1 to 1), the learning rate and the update every 2 ms are standard choices the paper does not give. The integrator with corrective feedback and the tamed-chaos network lack parameters in the text and are not built.

from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
t0 = time.time()
rows = []
for seed in range(10):
    sil = np.random.default_rng(100 + seed).choice(100, 50, replace=False)
    for name, fn in (("integrator, persistent input", lambda **k: L.simple_integrator(**k)),
                     ("integrator, transient input", lambda **k: L.simple_integrator(transient=True, **k)),
                     ("cascaded integrators, transient input", lambda **k: L.cascaded_integrator(**k))):
        _, o = fn(seed=seed); _, p = fn(seed=seed, silence=sil)
        sel = o[1][-1] - o[-1][-1]
        rows.append({"model": name, "seed": seed, "selectivity": sel,
                     "max_rel_diff": max(abs(p[1][-1] - o[1][-1]), abs(p[-1][-1] - o[-1][-1])) / abs(sel)})
with ProcessPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
    force = list(ex.map(L.force_test, range(10)))
for r in force:
    sel = r["unpert_right"] - r["unpert_left"]
    rows.append({"model": "FORCE network, transient input", "seed": r["seed"], "selectivity": sel,
                 "max_rel_diff": max(abs(r["pert_right"] - r["unpert_right"]), abs(r["pert_left"] - r["unpert_left"])) / abs(sel),
                 "train_err": r["train_err"]})
mono = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"simulated in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
print(mono.round(3).to_string(index=False))
ms = mono.groupby("model").agg(networks=("seed", "size"), min_rel_diff=("max_rel_diff", "min"), median_rel_diff=("max_rel_diff", "median"),
                               fail_to_recover=("max_rel_diff", lambda x: int((x > 0.1).sum())))
print("\n", ms.round(3).to_string())

Result: reproduced. Each of 10 simple integrators ends 20% to 22% of its selectivity away from its unperturbed output after silencing half of its units (persistent input), and each of 10 FORCE networks trained to ramp after a transient input ends 13% to 76% away (median 41%); all exceed the 10% bound. The transient-input and cascaded integrators end about 50% away. The two models whose parameters the text lacks were not built.

fig6-modular-models-recover¶

Modular networks of two coupled modules (attractor, integrator, trained recurrent network) recover after silencing of one module; the modular attractor drifts to a random fixed point when both modules are silenced.

Criterion: modular attractor and modular integrator with the Methods' parameters; 1 ms step with Euler-Maruyama as the standard choice before the answer. Reproduced when, over 100 simulated trials per trial type, the modular attractor ends at the instructed fixed point in more than 90% of trials after unilateral silencing and in 30% to 70% after bilateral silencing, and the modular integrator returns within 10% of its unperturbed trajectory by 2 s after unilateral silencing. Answered 2026-10-21 as not given by the paper: the noise, (n1) white noise of intensity 0.01, increment sd sqrt(0.01 dt)/tau, or (n2) one sample of variance 0.01 per step, integrated like an input; and the step, (h1) 1 ms or (h2) 0.1 ms. The outcome must hold under all four, else methods_underspecified. A trial ends at the instructed fixed point when both modules have the instructed unit above the other one at 2 s.

rows = []
STEPS = {"h1": 0.001, "h2": 0.0001}
for noise, nname in (("em", "n1"), ("sample", "n2")):
    for hname, dt in STEPS.items():
        for cond, sil in (("unperturbed", ()), ("unilateral", (0, 1)), ("bilateral", (0, 1, 2, 3))):
            ok = []
            for k, trial in enumerate(("right", "left")):
                _, R = L.modular_attractor(trial, silence=sil, seed=7 + k + 10 * len(sil), noise=noise, n_trials=100, dt=dt)
                end = R[:, -1]
                inst = (end[:, 0] > end[:, 1]) & (end[:, 2] > end[:, 3]) if trial == "right" else (end[:, 1] > end[:, 0]) & (end[:, 3] > end[:, 2])
                ok.append(inst)
            ok = np.concatenate(ok)
            rows.append({"noise": nname, "step": hname, "silencing": cond, "trials": len(ok), "instructed_fixed_point": ok.mean()})
att = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(att.to_string(index=False))
mi = []
for hname, dt in STEPS.items():
    for trial in ("right", "left"):
        _, R0 = L.modular_integrator(trial, dt=dt); _, R1 = L.modular_integrator(trial, silence=(0, 1, 2, 3), dt=dt)
        sel0 = R0[-1, 0] - R0[-1, 1]; sel1 = R1[-1, 0] - R1[-1, 1]
        sel0b = R0[-1, 4] - R0[-1, 5]; sel1b = R1[-1, 4] - R1[-1, 5]
        mi.append({"step": hname, "trial": trial, "module1_unperturbed": sel0, "module1_silenced": sel1, "rel_diff_module1": abs(sel1 - sel0) / abs(sel0),
                   "module2_unperturbed": sel0b, "module2_after": sel1b, "rel_diff_module2": abs(sel1b - sel0b) / abs(sel0b)})
mi = pd.DataFrame(mi)
print("\nModular integrator, right minus left integrator unit at 2 s, module 1 silenced 0.2-1.0 s:")
print(mi.round(4).to_string(index=False))
judge6 = []
for nname in ("n1", "n2"):
    for hname in STEPS:
        a = att[(att.noise == nname) & (att.step == hname)].set_index("silencing").instructed_fixed_point
        m = mi[mi.step == hname].set_index("trial").rel_diff_module1 <= 0.1
        parts = {"attractor_unilateral": bool(a["unilateral"] > 0.9), "attractor_bilateral": bool(0.3 <= a["bilateral"] <= 0.7),
                 "integrator_right": bool(m["right"]), "integrator_left": bool(m["left"])}
        judge6.append({"noise": nname, "step": hname, **parts,
                       "outcome_here": "reproduced" if all(parts.values()) else "partially" if any(parts.values()) else "not"})
judge6 = pd.DataFrame(judge6)
print("\n", judge6.to_string(index=False))

Result: partially reproduced. The answer leaves the noise (n1, n2) and the step (h1, h2) open, and the claims file requires one outcome over all four; all four give partial. Under n2 the modular attractor ends at the instructed fixed point in 100% of trials after unilateral silencing and in 48% (h1) or 50% (h2) after bilateral silencing, as the claim says. Under n1 the noise dominates: it ends there in 41.5% to 51% of trials whatever the silencing (51% and 48.5% unperturbed), so the unilateral part fails, and the bilateral fraction (43%, 44%) lies in the 30% to 70% band only because the network is at chance. The modular integrator with the printed matrix restores lick right trials (0.2% from unperturbed at 2 s with 1 ms steps, 5.4% with 0.1 ms steps) but not lick left ones (50% away under both steps): its recovery unit passes only right-preferring activity.

Blocked claims¶

  • fig1d-late-delay-ipsilateral-bias, fig1d-earlier-photoinhibition-minimal, ed3-behaviour-recovery-interval, fig2b-unilateral-performance, fig2b-bilateral-performance (data_missing). They rest on the behavioural photoinhibition sessions of 5 and 13 mice (photoinhibition on 25% of trials, light ending at the go cue, 1.3 s light with a variable delay, four-spot unilateral and two-spot bilateral protocols). The dandiset holds only the recording sessions (40% light trials), which lack those conditions (data check). The behaviour during the recordings is shown above for reference only: in experiment 1 (4 mice) performance on early-delay and late-delay photoinhibition trials is 0.745 and 0.749 against 0.799 in control (paired p 0.21 and 0.16), in line with fig1d-earlier-photoinhibition-minimal; in experiment 2 (7 mice) one spot with the hemispheres pooled gives 0.716 against 0.773 (paired p 0.059) and eight spots bilaterally 0.580 (paired p 0.0001); in experiment 3 (3 mice) one spot pooled gives 0.705, four spots 0.756 (left) and 0.830 (right), and two spots bilaterally 0.658 against 0.795 in control (paired p 0.045). These are other mice and sessions than the paper's behavioural cohort, with light on 40% of trials.
  • ed5-photoactivation-recovery, ed5-photoactivation-rate-changes (data_missing). No Tlx_PL56-cre x Ai32 mouse is in the dandiset (genotypes in the data check).
  • ed2d-spatial-extent (data_missing). The recordings of the 4 untrained mice are not in the dandiset.
  • ed9f-reaction-time (data_missing). The analysis ran in its own section above: the lick trace of the experiment-2 sessions holds no licks, so the reaction times the claim needs are not there.
  • fig5b-callosotomy-control-performance (data_missing). There are no sessions before the callosotomy, and no file marks the 7 mice as callosotomised.
  • fig5b-callosotomy-unilateral-sensitivity, ed10-callosotomy-preparatory-activity, fig5-callosotomy-no-recovery, fig5f-callosotomy-cd-reduced (metadata_insufficient). The 33 sessions of the 7 mice without a photostimulus record contain photoinhibition trials (silenced trials in the data check), but no file says which trials, where or when, so control and photoinhibition trials cannot be told apart. They hold 519 putative pyramidal units (paper 496, within tolerance, if these are the callosotomy mice, which no file says). Counted on all their trials, photoinhibition trials included, 331 to 340 are selective with correct trials (paper 254 on control trials) and 81 to 84 in the sample epoch (cell below); this is not the claim's measure.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. Conditions are read from the laser traces and events, as the trial table has none. Session 258250_20141202 (interleaved, overlapping trial sequences) and the three experiment-1 sessions without a photostimulus record are left out of trial-based analyses. Details the claims file leaves open are run under each reading. The answers of 2026-10-21 to the ten questions asked found every detail missing from the paper; the readings they name are run, and a claim whose method-detail readings disagree is blocked. This changed two outcomes: cd-captures-selectivity (not reproduced before) is blocked, as its v1 and v2 readings differ, and ed9f-reaction-time, blocked before for want of a lick rule, was run over a range of thresholds and is blocked because the lick trace holds no licks. Several counts of included neurons and sessions differ from the paper's (55 and 143 neurons for the recovery times against 138 to 173 and 221 to 293 here; 16 sessions with 6 to 20 neurons for the activity space against 24 with 6 to 37), so the paper's selections are not those of the claims file. The simulations use standard choices for the integration step, the FORCE target and feedback, and the seeds; the modular attractor is run with both noise readings and both steps the answer names. Photoinhibition-trial random splits use one seed per session.

Partial outcomes. Where a criterion defines no partial outcome (unit-classification, selective-fraction, ed2b-silencing-strength, fig2-recordings-recovery, ed7e, ed8 and fig6), a claim that is not reproduced is called partially reproduced when at least half of the parts of its criterion hold under every reading that must agree (K1 and K2, and the other method details), and not reproduced otherwise. This rule was written after the first verification round, where the verifier judged several of these claims not reproduced; it moved selective-fraction (one count of four under K1) and ed2b-silencing-strength (one part of four under K2) to not reproduced, and leaves unit-classification (four of five), fig2-recordings-recovery (three of five), ed7e-roc-larger-photoinhibition and ed8-roc-during-photoinhibition (three of four under K1, two under K2) and fig6-modular-models-recover (two or three of four) partial.

After the first verification round. cd-stable-over-epochs is blocked: w from all correct control trials gives 0.563 and 0.588, inside the band, and w from the training subset 0.534 to 0.554, outside, and the claims file fixes neither. Under K2, 3% to 16% of the trials of each photoinhibition condition of experiment 1, 6.5% to 7.5% in experiment 2 and 1% to 4% in experiment 3 have their light before its logged time, so K2 mixes trials without light into the photoinhibition averages (data check); the claims file defines K2 with events at their logged times, and a question asks whether that is meant.

What was found about the dandiset. It holds the recordings of the paper's 12 control mice (58 sessions, 890 putative pyramidal units as in the paper) and 33 sessions of 7 further mice that match the callosotomy experiment, but not the behavioural photoinhibition sessions, the photoactivation and untrained mice, or any session before callosotomy. About 33 units of intermediate spike width are missing (15 against 50). The photostimulus is not in the trial table; it is recorded as laser traces per site and events, from which the site, the number of spots and the timing can be read, but in 36 sessions (the 33 of the callosotomy mice and 3 of experiment 1) it is missing although those sessions contain silenced trials. No file says which mice were callosotomised. In lick-early trials the photostimulus event is logged at the restarted delay; in 339 of 931 such trials it lies more than 0.1 s after the light, which came up to 10 s before the logged go cue. One session has interleaved overlapping trial sequences; 28 units have spike times out of time order; the files' cell_type labels intermediate-width units as FS; the behaviour-only file is empty. No file holds lick times: the lick_trace of the 24 experiment-2 sessions used for the activity space stays within about 0.002 of its baseline when the mouse licks, so licks cannot be read from it, while the experiment-3 and unlabelled sessions read as references do carry licks.
